docs.text:
incident_registry(incidents: DataFrame | Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None) -> DataFrame

Validate incidents and return them as a registry frame (INCIDENT_COLUMNS).

incidents is a frame or an iterable of dicts with the registry's keys. scope defaults to "all" and end_utc to ongoing; times are read as UTC. A problem raises GBFSValidationError (unknown cause, duplicated id, end before start).

Examples:

>>> reg = incident_registry([{
...     "incident_id": "power-cut", "start_utc": "2026-03-02T10:00Z",
...     "end_utc": "2026-03-02T14:00Z", "cause": "outage_collector",
...     "summary": "Power cut at the collection site."}])
>>> reg.loc[0, ["incident_id", "scope", "cause"]].tolist()
['power-cut', 'all', 'outage_collector']
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def incident_registry(
    incidents: pd.DataFrame | Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Validate incidents and return them as a registry frame (`INCIDENT_COLUMNS`).

    ``incidents`` is a frame or an iterable of dicts with the registry's keys. ``scope`` defaults
    to ``"all"`` and ``end_utc`` to *ongoing*; times are read as UTC. A problem raises
    ``GBFSValidationError`` (unknown cause, duplicated id, end before start).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> reg = incident_registry([{
    ...     "incident_id": "power-cut", "start_utc": "2026-03-02T10:00Z",
    ...     "end_utc": "2026-03-02T14:00Z", "cause": "outage_collector",
    ...     "summary": "Power cut at the collection site."}])
    >>> reg.loc[0, ["incident_id", "scope", "cause"]].tolist()
    ['power-cut', 'all', 'outage_collector']
    """
    if incidents is None:
        return _empty_registry()
    df = incidents.copy() if isinstance(incidents, pd.DataFrame) else pd.DataFrame(list(incidents))
    if df.empty:
        return _empty_registry()
    need_columns(df, ["incident_id", "start_utc", "cause"], what="incident_registry")
    for col, default in (("end_utc", pd.NaT), ("scope", "all"), ("summary", "")):
        if col not in df.columns:
            df[col] = default
    df = df[INCIDENT_COLUMNS].copy()
    df["start_utc"] = to_utc(df["start_utc"], what="start_utc")
    df["end_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(df["end_utc"].replace("", None), utc=True, format="mixed")
    df["scope"] = df["scope"].fillna("all").replace("", "all").astype("string")
    df["incident_id"] = df["incident_id"].astype("string")
    df["cause"] = df["cause"].astype("string")
    df["summary"] = df["summary"].fillna("").astype("string")
    bad = sorted(set(df["cause"]) - set(CAUSES))
    if bad:
        raise GBFSValidationError(f"unknown incident cause(s) {bad}; expected one of {CAUSES}")
    dup = df["incident_id"][df["incident_id"].duplicated()].tolist()
    if dup:
        raise GBFSValidationError(f"duplicated incident_id: {sorted(set(dup))}")
    backwards = df["end_utc"].notna() & (df["end_utc"] < df["start_utc"])
    if backwards.any():
        raise GBFSValidationError(
            f"incident(s) {df.loc[backwards, 'incident_id'].tolist()} end before they start"
        )
    return df.sort_values(["start_utc", "incident_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)

def add_incident(
    registry: pd.DataFrame | None,
    incident_id: str,
    start: str | pd.Timestamp,
    end: str | pd.Timestamp | None = None,
    *,
    cause: str,
    scope: str = "all",
    summary: str = "",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """A new registry that holds ``registry`` plus one incident (the input is not modified).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> reg = add_incident(None, "site-move", "2026-03-02", "2026-03-03",
    ...                    cause="outage_collector", summary="Moved the collector.")
    >>> len(add_incident(reg, "feed-down", "2026-03-05", cause="outage_operator", scope="demo"))
    2
    """
    row = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {
                "incident_id": incident_id,
                "start_utc": start,
                "end_utc": end if end is not None else pd.NaT,
                "scope": scope,
                "cause": cause,
                "summary": summary,
            }
        ]
    )
    return incident_registry(pd.concat([incident_registry(registry), row], ignore_index=True))

write_incidents(registry: DataFrame, path: str | Path) -> Path

Write the registry as .json (a list of objects) or .csv, by the file suffix.

Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC (2026-03-02T10:00:00Z); an ongoing incident has a null end_utc in JSON and an empty cell in CSV.

Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def write_incidents(registry: pd.DataFrame, path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Write the registry as ``.json`` (a list of objects) or ``.csv``, by the file suffix.

    Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC (``2026-03-02T10:00:00Z``); an ongoing incident has a null
    ``end_utc`` in JSON and an empty cell in CSV.
    """
    out = Path(path)
    reg = incident_registry(registry)
    records = [
        {
            "incident_id": str(r.incident_id),
            "start_utc": _iso(r.start_utc),
            "end_utc": _iso(r.end_utc),
            "scope": str(r.scope),
            "cause": str(r.cause),
            "summary": str(r.summary),
        }
        for r in reg.itertuples(index=False)
    ]
    suffix = out.suffix.lower()
    if suffix not in (".json", ".csv"):
        raise ValueError(f"write_incidents: use a .json or .csv path, got {out.name!r}")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if suffix == ".json":
        out.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        pd.DataFrame(records, columns=INCIDENT_COLUMNS).to_csv(out, index=False)
    return out

def read_incidents(path: str | Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Read a registry written by `write_incidents` (``.json`` or ``.csv``)."""
    p = Path(path)
    suffix = p.suffix.lower()
    if suffix == ".json":
        return incident_registry(json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    if suffix == ".csv":
        return incident_registry(pd.read_csv(p, keep_default_na=False))
    raise ValueError(f"read_incidents: use a .json or .csv path, got {p.name!r}")

incidents_overlapping(registry: DataFrame, start: str | Timestamp, end: str | Timestamp, systems: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> DataFrame

The incidents that overlap [start, end) and touch systems (all, when None).

An incident with scope "all" touches every system; an ongoing one never ends.

Examples:

>>> reg = incident_registry([
...     {"incident_id": "a", "start_utc": "2026-03-01", "end_utc": "2026-03-02",
...      "cause": "outage_collector"},
...     {"incident_id": "b", "start_utc": "2026-04-01", "cause": "outage_operator",
...      "scope": "demo"}])
>>> incidents_overlapping(reg, "2026-03-01", "2026-03-10")["incident_id"].tolist()
['a']
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def incidents_overlapping(
    registry: pd.DataFrame,
    start: str | pd.Timestamp,
    end: str | pd.Timestamp,
    systems: Iterable[str] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The incidents that overlap ``[start, end)`` and touch ``systems`` (all, when ``None``).

    An incident with scope ``"all"`` touches every system; an ongoing one never ends.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> reg = incident_registry([
    ...     {"incident_id": "a", "start_utc": "2026-03-01", "end_utc": "2026-03-02",
    ...      "cause": "outage_collector"},
    ...     {"incident_id": "b", "start_utc": "2026-04-01", "cause": "outage_operator",
    ...      "scope": "demo"}])
    >>> incidents_overlapping(reg, "2026-03-01", "2026-03-10")["incident_id"].tolist()
    ['a']
    """
    reg = incident_registry(registry)
    if reg.empty:
        return reg
    lo, hi = to_utc([start]).iloc[0], to_utc([end]).iloc[0]
    wanted = None if systems is None else set(systems)
    keep = []
    for r in reg.itertuples(index=False):
        ends = _FAR_FUTURE if pd.isna(r.end_utc) else r.end_utc
        scope = _scope_systems(str(r.scope))
        touches = scope is None or wanted is None or bool(scope & wanted)
        keep.append(bool(r.start_utc < hi and ends > lo and touches))
    return reg[np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)].reset_index(drop=True)

When every system goes quiet together, the cause is the collection, not the operators. Polls are compared at one-minute resolution. known is a registry: the time it already explains with outage_collector incidents is subtracted, and only the stretches that remain and last at least min_gap are reported.

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> t = pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01T00:00Z", "2026-03-01T00:01Z", "2026-03-01T05:00Z"])
>>> gaps = find_collector_gaps(pd.DataFrame({"fetched_at": t}))
>>> str(gaps.loc[0, "duration"])
'0 days 04:58:00'
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def find_collector_gaps(
    snapshots: Any,
    *,
    min_gap: str | pd.Timedelta = DEFAULT_MIN_GAP,
    known: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    time_col: str = "fetched_at",
    engine: str = "auto",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Stretches in which **no system at all** was polled for ``min_gap`` or more.

    When every system goes quiet together, the cause is the collection, not the operators.
    Polls are compared at one-minute resolution. ``known`` is a registry: the time it already
    explains with ``outage_collector`` incidents is subtracted, and only the stretches that
    remain and last at least ``min_gap`` are reported.

    ``snapshots`` is a frame, an Arrow table, a DuckDB relation or a path (see
    `daily_coverage` for ``engine``).

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        ``start_utc, end_utc, duration`` (a ``Timedelta``), one row per gap.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> t = pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01T00:00Z", "2026-03-01T00:01Z", "2026-03-01T05:00Z"])
    >>> gaps = find_collector_gaps(pd.DataFrame({"fetched_at": t}))
    >>> str(gaps.loc[0, "duration"])
    '0 days 04:58:00'
    """
    table = _source(snapshots, time_col, [], "find_collector_gaps")
    gap = fixed_timedelta(min_gap, what="min_gap")
    use = resolve_engine(engine, table, what="find_collector_gaps")
    minutes = _distinct_minutes(table, use, time_col)
    declared = _intervals(incident_registry(known), "outage_collector")
    return _gaps_from_minutes(minutes, gap, declared)

daily_coverage(snapshots: Any, *, expected_polls: int | None = None, ok_threshold_pct: float = DEFAULT_OK_THRESHOLD_PCT, poll_resolution: str | Timedelta = '1min', known_incidents: DataFrame | None = None, min_collector_gap: str | Timedelta = DEFAULT_MIN_GAP, start: str | Timestamp | None = None, end: str | Timestamp | None = None, time_col: str = 'fetched_at', engine: str = 'auto') -> DataFrame

Per system and UTC day: polls expected and obtained, completeness and a status.

A poll is a distinct poll_resolution slot (a minute by default) in which the system has at least one row. expected_polls defaults to the number of slots in a day (1440 for a poll every minute; pass poll_resolution="15min" for 96).

The window of each system starts on its first day; start and end (UTC days, inclusive) bound it. By default end is the last day present in the data, so a day still being collected counts as partial: pass yesterday's date to leave it out. Days with no row at all between a system's first day and end are reported with zero polls.

known_incidents (a registry) and the gaps found in snapshots explain missing polls as outage_collector; a declared outage_operator incident of a system explains its own.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default snapshots pandas.DataFrame, pyarrow.Table, duckdb relation, str or Path

One row per station (or vehicle) per poll, with system_id and time_col (tz-aware UTC; naive is read as UTC). num_bikes_available and num_docks_available add both_zero_pct. A table, a relation or a path (a lake written by gbfs_toolkit.store, a folder of Parquet files, a file or a glob) is summarised without loading it whole; its time column must be a timestamp.

required engine ('auto', 'duckdb', 'pandas')

Who computes. A pandas frame stays on pandas under "auto"; any other source goes to DuckDB when the duckdb extra is installed, and is otherwise read in batches by pandas (memory: the polls, not the rows). The engines give the same table.

"auto" ok_threshold_pct float

Completeness from which a day is ok.

95.0

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

COVERAGE_COLUMNS. units_reporting_median is the median number of rows per poll (stations or vehicles published); both_zero_pct the share of the day's rows at zero bikes and zero docks, in the raw values you passed.

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> t = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=1440, freq="min", tz="UTC")
>>> full = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "a", "fetched_at": t})
>>> half = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "b", "fetched_at": t[:700]})
>>> cov = daily_coverage(pd.concat([full, half]))
>>> dict(zip(cov["system_id"], cov["status"]))
{'a': 'ok', 'b': 'partial'}
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def daily_coverage(
    snapshots: Any,
    *,
    expected_polls: int | None = None,
    ok_threshold_pct: float = DEFAULT_OK_THRESHOLD_PCT,
    poll_resolution: str | pd.Timedelta = "1min",
    known_incidents: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    min_collector_gap: str | pd.Timedelta = DEFAULT_MIN_GAP,
    start: str | pd.Timestamp | None = None,
    end: str | pd.Timestamp | None = None,
    time_col: str = "fetched_at",
    engine: str = "auto",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per system and UTC day: polls expected and obtained, completeness and a status.

    A *poll* is a distinct ``poll_resolution`` slot (a minute by default) in which the system has
    at least one row. ``expected_polls`` defaults to the number of slots in a day (1440 for a
    poll every minute; pass ``poll_resolution="15min"`` for 96).

    The window of each system starts on its first day; ``start`` and ``end`` (UTC days,
    inclusive) bound it. By default ``end`` is the last day present in the data, so **a day
    still being collected counts as partial**: pass yesterday's date to leave it out. Days with
    no row at all between a system's first day and ``end`` are reported with zero polls.

    ``known_incidents`` (a registry) and the gaps found in ``snapshots`` explain missing polls
    as ``outage_collector``; a declared ``outage_operator`` incident of a system explains its own.

    Parameters
    ----------
    snapshots : pandas.DataFrame, pyarrow.Table, duckdb relation, str or Path
        One row per station (or vehicle) per poll, with ``system_id`` and ``time_col``
        (tz-aware UTC; naive is read as UTC). ``num_bikes_available`` and
        ``num_docks_available`` add ``both_zero_pct``. A table, a relation or a path (a lake
        written by `gbfs_toolkit.store`, a folder of Parquet files, a file or a glob) is
        summarised without loading it whole; its time column must be a timestamp.
    engine : {"auto", "duckdb", "pandas"}, default "auto"
        Who computes. A pandas frame stays on pandas under ``"auto"``; any other source goes
        to DuckDB when the ``duckdb`` extra is installed, and is otherwise read in batches by
        pandas (memory: the polls, not the rows). The engines give the same table.
    ok_threshold_pct : float, default 95.0
        Completeness from which a day is ``ok``.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `COVERAGE_COLUMNS`. ``units_reporting_median`` is the median number of rows per
        poll (stations or vehicles published); ``both_zero_pct`` the share of the day's rows at
        zero bikes and zero docks, in the raw values you passed.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> t = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=1440, freq="min", tz="UTC")
    >>> full = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "a", "fetched_at": t})
    >>> half = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "b", "fetched_at": t[:700]})
    >>> cov = daily_coverage(pd.concat([full, half]))
    >>> dict(zip(cov["system_id"], cov["status"]))
    {'a': 'ok', 'b': 'partial'}
    """
    table = _source(snapshots, time_col, ["system_id"], "daily_coverage")
    step = fixed_timedelta(poll_resolution, what="poll_resolution")
    expected = int(_DAY / step) if expected_polls is None else int(expected_polls)
    if expected <= 0:
        raise ValueError("expected_polls must be positive")
    if not 0 < ok_threshold_pct <= 100:
        raise ValueError("ok_threshold_pct must be in (0, 100]")
    use = resolve_engine(engine, table, what="daily_coverage")

    reg = incident_registry(known_incidents)
    first_day = _as_day(start)
    lo = None if first_day is None else pd.Timestamp(first_day, tz="UTC")
    span = table.time_range(time_col)
    if span is None or (lo is not None and span[1] < lo):
        return _empty_coverage()
    last_day = _as_day(end) or span[1].date()
    hi = pd.Timestamp(last_day, tz="UTC") + _DAY
    lo_us = None if lo is None else int((lo - _EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(microseconds=1))
    hi_us = int((hi - _EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(microseconds=1))

    observed, has_counts = _poll_counts(table, use, time_col, step, lo_us, hi_us)
    if observed.empty:
        return _empty_coverage()
    minutes = _distinct_minutes(table, use, time_col, lo_us, hi_us)
    gaps = _gaps_from_minutes(
        minutes,
        fixed_timedelta(min_collector_gap, what="min_gap"),
        _intervals(reg, "outage_collector"),
    )
    gap_intervals: list[_Interval] = list(zip(gaps["start_utc"], gaps["end_utc"], strict=True))

    out_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for system, sub in observed.groupby(level="system_id", sort=True):
        days = sub.droplevel("system_id")
        d = min(days.index)
        collector = gap_intervals + _intervals(reg, "outage_collector", str(system))
        operator = _intervals(reg, "outage_operator", str(system))
        while d <= last_day:
            t0 = pd.Timestamp(d, tz="UTC")
            n_polls, median_rows, share = 0, None, None
            if d in days.index:
                row = days.loc[d]
                n_polls, median_rows = int(row["n_polls"]), float(row["median_rows"])
                if has_counts and row["rows"]:
                    share = round(100 * float(row["zeros"]) / float(row["rows"]), 2)
            pct = round(100 * min(n_polls, expected) / expected, 1)
            if pct >= ok_threshold_pct:
                status = STATUS_OK
            elif _overlaps(collector, t0, t0 + _DAY):
                status = STATUS_OUTAGE_COLLECTOR
            elif n_polls == 0 or _overlaps(operator, t0, t0 + _DAY):
                status = STATUS_OUTAGE_OPERATOR
            else:
                status = STATUS_PARTIAL
            out_rows.append(
                {
                    "date_utc": d,
                    "system_id": system,
                    "expected_polls": expected,
                    "actual_polls": n_polls,
                    "completeness_pct": pct,
                    "units_reporting_median": median_rows,
                    "both_zero_pct": share,
                    "status": status,
                }
            )
            d += dt.timedelta(days=1)
    out = pd.DataFrame(out_rows, columns=COVERAGE_COLUMNS)
    out["expected_polls"] = out["expected_polls"].astype("int64")
    out["actual_polls"] = out["actual_polls"].astype("int64")
    for c in ("completeness_pct", "units_reporting_median", "both_zero_pct"):
        out[c] = out[c].astype("float64")
    _log.info("coverage: %d system-days, %s", len(out), out["status"].value_counts().to_dict())
    return out

docs.text:
find_silent_feeds(coverage: DataFrame) -> DataFrame

Runs of consecutive outage_operator days per system: feeds that went silent.

The collection was running (otherwise the days would be outage_collector), yet the operator's feed gave nothing. A run that reaches the last day of coverage is ongoing (end_utc is NaT).

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

system_id, start_utc, end_utc, n_days.

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> cov = pd.DataFrame({
...     "date_utc": pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01", "2026-03-02", "2026-03-03"]).date,
...     "system_id": "a",
...     "status": ["ok", "outage_operator", "outage_operator"]})
>>> silent = find_silent_feeds(cov)
>>> int(silent.loc[0, "n_days"]), bool(pd.isna(silent.loc[0, "end_utc"]))
(2, True)
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def find_silent_feeds(coverage: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Runs of consecutive ``outage_operator`` days per system: feeds that went silent.

    The collection was running (otherwise the days would be ``outage_collector``), yet the
    operator's feed gave nothing. A run that reaches the last day of ``coverage`` is *ongoing*
    (``end_utc`` is ``NaT``).

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        ``system_id, start_utc, end_utc, n_days``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> cov = pd.DataFrame({
    ...     "date_utc": pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01", "2026-03-02", "2026-03-03"]).date,
    ...     "system_id": "a",
    ...     "status": ["ok", "outage_operator", "outage_operator"]})
    >>> silent = find_silent_feeds(cov)
    >>> int(silent.loc[0, "n_days"]), bool(pd.isna(silent.loc[0, "end_utc"]))
    (2, True)
    """
    need_columns(coverage, ["date_utc", "system_id", "status"], what="find_silent_feeds")
    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    if len(coverage):
        last = max(coverage["date_utc"])
        for system, sub in coverage.sort_values("date_utc").groupby("system_id", sort=True):
            run: list[dt.date] = []
            days = list(zip(sub["date_utc"], sub["status"], strict=True))
            for i, (d, status) in enumerate(days):
                silent = status == STATUS_OUTAGE_OPERATOR
                if silent:
                    run.append(d)
                if run and (not silent or i == len(days) - 1):
                    ongoing = silent and run[-1] == last
                    out.append(
                        {
                            "system_id": system,
                            "start_utc": pd.Timestamp(run[0], tz="UTC"),
                            "end_utc": pd.NaT
                            if ongoing
                            else pd.Timestamp(run[-1], tz="UTC") + _DAY,
                            "n_days": len(run),
                        }
                    )
                    run = []
    res = pd.DataFrame(out, columns=["system_id", "start_utc", "end_utc", "n_days"])
    res["start_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(res["start_utc"], utc=True)
    res["end_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(res["end_utc"], utc=True)
    return res

detect_incidents(coverage: DataFrame, snapshots: Any = None, *, known: DataFrame | None = None, min_collector_gap: str | Timedelta = DEFAULT_MIN_GAP, time_col: str = 'fetched_at', engine: str = 'auto') -> DataFrame

The registry completed with what the data shows: collection gaps and silent feeds.

Your declared incidents (known) come first. With snapshots, every find_collector_gaps stretch is added as collector-gap-<start> (cause outage_collector); every find_silent_feeds run is added as silent-<system>-<day> (cause outage_operator). Identifiers are stable: running it again on the same data gives the same registry.

Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def detect_incidents(
    coverage: pd.DataFrame,
    snapshots: Any = None,
    *,
    known: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    min_collector_gap: str | pd.Timedelta = DEFAULT_MIN_GAP,
    time_col: str = "fetched_at",
    engine: str = "auto",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The registry completed with what the data shows: collection gaps and silent feeds.

    Your declared incidents (``known``) come first. With ``snapshots``, every
    `find_collector_gaps` stretch is added as ``collector-gap-<start>`` (cause
    ``outage_collector``); every `find_silent_feeds` run is added as
    ``silent-<system>-<day>`` (cause ``outage_operator``). Identifiers are stable: running it
    again on the same data gives the same registry.
    """
    reg = incident_registry(known)
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    if snapshots is not None:
        gaps = find_collector_gaps(
            snapshots, min_gap=min_collector_gap, known=reg, time_col=time_col, engine=engine
        )
        for g in gaps.itertuples(index=False):
            rows.append(
                {
                    "incident_id": f"collector-gap-{g.start_utc:%Y%m%dT%H%M}Z",
                    "start_utc": g.start_utc,
                    "end_utc": g.end_utc,
                    "scope": "all",
                    "cause": "outage_collector",
                    "summary": (
                        f"No snapshot from any system for {_fmt_duration(g.duration)} "
                        "(collection gap detected; cause not documented)."
                    ),
                }
            )
    for s in find_silent_feeds(coverage).itertuples(index=False):
        ongoing = pd.isna(s.end_utc)
        plural = "s" if s.n_days > 1 else ""
        rows.append(
            {
                "incident_id": f"silent-{s.system_id}-{s.start_utc:%Y%m%d}",
                "start_utc": s.start_utc,
                "end_utc": pd.NaT if ongoing else s.end_utc,
                "scope": s.system_id,
                "cause": "outage_operator",
                "summary": (
                    f"No snapshot from {s.system_id} for {s.n_days} day{plural}"
                    f"{' (ongoing)' if ongoing else ''} while the collection was running: "
                    "the operator's feed was silent or failing (detected)."
                ),
            }
        )
    both = pd.concat([reg, incident_registry(rows)], ignore_index=True)
    return incident_registry(both.drop_duplicates("incident_id"))

assess(snapshots: Any, *, known_incidents: DataFrame | None = None, time_col: str = 'fetched_at', **coverage_options: Any) -> QualityReport

Coverage and incidents in one call: daily_coverage then detect_incidents.

snapshots is a frame, an Arrow table, a DuckDB relation or a path (a lake, a folder of Parquet files), summarised without loading it whole; coverage_options are the options of daily_coverage (expected_polls, ok_threshold_pct, end, engine ...).

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> t = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=1440, freq="min", tz="UTC")
>>> report = assess(pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "demo", "fetched_at": t}))
>>> report.summary()["days_by_status"]["ok"]
1
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def assess(
    snapshots: Any,
    *,
    known_incidents: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    time_col: str = "fetched_at",
    **coverage_options: Any,
) -> QualityReport:
    """Coverage and incidents in one call: `daily_coverage` then `detect_incidents`.

    ``snapshots`` is a frame, an Arrow table, a DuckDB relation or a path (a lake, a folder of
    Parquet files), summarised without loading it whole; ``coverage_options`` are the options
    of `daily_coverage` (``expected_polls``, ``ok_threshold_pct``, ``end``, ``engine`` ...).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> t = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=1440, freq="min", tz="UTC")
    >>> report = assess(pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "demo", "fetched_at": t}))
    >>> report.summary()["days_by_status"]["ok"]
    1
    """
    table = _source(snapshots, time_col, ["system_id"], "assess")
    cov = daily_coverage(
        table, known_incidents=known_incidents, time_col=time_col, **coverage_options
    )
    inc = detect_incidents(
        cov,
        table,
        known=known_incidents,
        min_collector_gap=coverage_options.get("min_collector_gap", DEFAULT_MIN_GAP),
        time_col=time_col,
        engine=coverage_options.get("engine", "auto"),
    )
    return QualityReport(cov, inc)

docs.text:
field_unsupported_by_operator(df: Any, *, columns: tuple[str, ...] = _COUNT_COLS, period: str = 'M', time_col: str = 'fetched_at', engine: str = 'auto') -> DataFrame

Fields an operator does not publish: 0 in every non-empty value of the period.

A system with no docks reports num_docks_available = 0 everywhere. If every non-empty value of a column is 0 for a system over a period (a UTC month, "M", by default; "D" a day; "all" the whole frame), the column carries no information.

df is a frame, an Arrow table, a DuckDB relation or a path; see daily_coverage for engine.

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

system_id, period_start_utc, field, one row per unsupported (system, period, field).

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({
...     "system_id": "a", "fetched_at": pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01T00:00Z"] * 3),
...     "num_bikes_available": [3, 0, 5], "num_docks_available": [0, 0, 0]})
>>> field_unsupported_by_operator(df)["field"].tolist()
['num_docks_available']
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def field_unsupported_by_operator(
    df: Any,
    *,
    columns: tuple[str, ...] = _COUNT_COLS,
    period: str = "M",
    time_col: str = "fetched_at",
    engine: str = "auto",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fields an operator does not publish: ``0`` in every non-empty value of the period.

    A system with no docks reports ``num_docks_available = 0`` everywhere. If every non-empty
    value of a column is ``0`` for a system over a ``period`` (a UTC month, ``"M"``, by default;
    ``"D"`` a day; ``"all"`` the whole frame), the column carries no information.

    ``df`` is a frame, an Arrow table, a DuckDB relation or a path; see `daily_coverage` for
    ``engine``.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        ``system_id, period_start_utc, field``, one row per unsupported (system, period, field).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> df = pd.DataFrame({
    ...     "system_id": "a", "fetched_at": pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01T00:00Z"] * 3),
    ...     "num_bikes_available": [3, 0, 5], "num_docks_available": [0, 0, 0]})
    >>> field_unsupported_by_operator(df)["field"].tolist()
    ['num_docks_available']
    """
    table = _source(df, time_col, ["system_id"], "field_unsupported_by_operator")
    use = resolve_engine(engine, table, what="field_unsupported_by_operator")
    present = [c for c in columns if c in table.columns()]
    counts = _unsupported_counts(table, use, present, period, time_col)
    rows = [
        {
            "system_id": r.system_id,
            "period_start_utc": _period_start(int(r.key), period),
            "field": r.field,
        }
        for r in counts[counts["n"] == counts["z"]].itertuples(index=False)
    ]
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["system_id", "period_start_utc", "field"])
    out["period_start_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(out["period_start_utc"], utc=True)
    return out.sort_values(["system_id", "period_start_utc", "field"]).reset_index(drop=True)

docs.text:
add_quality_indicators(df: DataFrame, *, capacity: DataFrame | None = None, period: str = 'M', all_zero_share: float = DEFAULT_ALL_ZERO_SHARE, mask_unsupported: bool = True, time_col: str = 'fetched_at') -> DataFrame

Add the three ambiguity indicators to station-status rows (a copy; no row is removed).

field_unsupported_by_operator <NA>, or the comma-separated fields the operator does not publish in the row's period (see field_unsupported_by_operator). With mask_unsupported (the default) those columns are set to missing in the returned frame, so a column of placeholders is not mistaken for data. both_zero_suspect True for a row with zero bikes, zero free docks and a positive capacity; False when its counts say otherwise; <NA> when a count or the capacity is missing (so also for a masked column or an unknown capacity). network_all_zero_anomaly True when, in the row's poll (system and time), more than all_zero_share of all rows are at zero on every field the operator publishes; <NA> when it publishes neither field.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default df DataFrame

system_id, station_id, time_col and the two count columns.

required capacity DataFrame

station_id and capacity (and system_id when ids repeat across systems). If omitted, a capacity column of df is used.

None

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> t = pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01T10:00Z"] * 3)
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({
...     "system_id": "a", "station_id": ["s1", "s2", "s3"], "fetched_at": t,
...     "num_bikes_available": [0, 4, 2], "num_docks_available": [0, 6, 0],
...     "capacity": [10, 10, 10]})
>>> add_quality_indicators(df)["both_zero_suspect"].tolist()
[True, False, False]
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/quality.py 
def add_quality_indicators(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    capacity: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    period: str = "M",
    all_zero_share: float = DEFAULT_ALL_ZERO_SHARE,
    mask_unsupported: bool = True,
    time_col: str = "fetched_at",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Add the three ambiguity indicators to station-status rows (a copy; no row is removed).

    ``field_unsupported_by_operator``
        ``<NA>``, or the comma-separated fields the operator does not publish in the row's
        period (see `field_unsupported_by_operator`). With ``mask_unsupported`` (the
        default) those columns are set to missing in the returned frame, so a column of
        placeholders is not mistaken for data.
    ``both_zero_suspect``
        ``True`` for a row with zero bikes, zero free docks and a positive capacity; ``False``
        when its counts say otherwise; ``<NA>`` when a count or the capacity is missing (so also
        for a masked column or an unknown capacity).
    ``network_all_zero_anomaly``
        ``True`` when, in the row's poll (system and time), more than ``all_zero_share`` of all
        rows are at zero on every field the operator publishes; ``<NA>`` when it publishes
        neither field.

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pandas.DataFrame
        ``system_id``, ``station_id``, ``time_col`` and the two count columns.
    capacity : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        ``station_id`` and ``capacity`` (and ``system_id`` when ids repeat across systems). If
        omitted, a ``capacity`` column of ``df`` is used.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> t = pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01T10:00Z"] * 3)
    >>> df = pd.DataFrame({
    ...     "system_id": "a", "station_id": ["s1", "s2", "s3"], "fetched_at": t,
    ...     "num_bikes_available": [0, 4, 2], "num_docks_available": [0, 6, 0],
    ...     "capacity": [10, 10, 10]})
    >>> add_quality_indicators(df)["both_zero_suspect"].tolist()
    [True, False, False]
    """
    if not is_pandas(df):
        raise TypeError(
            "add_quality_indicators returns one row per input row, so it takes a pandas DataFrame "
            "(read the part you need with gbfs_toolkit.store.read_lake first); "
            f"got {type(df).__name__}"
        )
    need_columns(df, ["system_id", "station_id", time_col], what="add_quality_indicators")
    if not 0 < all_zero_share <= 1:
        raise ValueError("all_zero_share must be in (0, 1]")
    out = df.copy()
    system = out["system_id"].astype(str)
    times = to_utc(out[time_col], what=time_col)
    present = [c for c in _COUNT_COLS if c in out.columns]
    key = _period_key(times, period)
    raw = {c: pd.to_numeric(out[c], errors="coerce") for c in present}

    unsupported = field_unsupported_by_operator(
        out, columns=tuple(present), period=period, time_col=time_col
    )
    muted: dict[str, pd.Series] = {}
    names: list[pd.Series] = []
    for col in present:
        sub = unsupported[unsupported["field"] == col]
        starts = _period_key(sub["period_start_utc"], period)
        pairs = set(zip(sub["system_id"], starts, strict=True))
        is_muted = pd.Series(
            [(s, int(k)) in pairs for s, k in zip(system, key, strict=True)],
            index=out.index,
            dtype=bool,
        )
        muted[col] = is_muted
        names.append(pd.Series(np.where(is_muted, col, ""), index=out.index, dtype="object"))
    flag_text = (
        pd.concat(names, axis=1).apply(lambda r: ",".join(v for v in r if v), axis=1)
        if names
        else pd.Series("", index=out.index, dtype="object")
    )

    # A poll's zero share: rows at zero on every published field / all rows of the poll.
    if present:
        zero_row = pd.Series(True, index=out.index)
        nothing_published = pd.Series(True, index=out.index)
        for c in present:
            zero_row &= (raw[c] == 0).fillna(False).astype(bool) | muted[c]
            nothing_published &= muted[c]
        zero_row &= ~nothing_published
        poll = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": system, "t": times, "z": zero_row.astype(float)})
        share = poll.groupby(["system_id", "t"], sort=False)["z"].transform("mean")
        anomaly = (share > all_zero_share).astype("boolean")
        anomaly[nothing_published] = pd.NA
    else:
        anomaly = pd.Series(pd.NA, index=out.index, dtype="boolean")

    if mask_unsupported:
        for c in present:
            if muted[c].any():
                out[c] = out[c].astype("Float64" if out[c].dtype.kind == "f" else out[c].dtype)
                out[c] = out[c].mask(muted[c])

    cap: pd.Series | None = None
    if capacity is not None:
        need_columns(capacity, ["station_id", "capacity"], what="add_quality_indicators(capacity)")
        keys = ["system_id", "station_id"] if "system_id" in capacity.columns else ["station_id"]
        cmap = capacity[[*keys, "capacity"]].drop_duplicates(keys).copy()
        for k in keys:
            cmap[k] = cmap[k].astype(str)
        left = pd.DataFrame(
            {"system_id": system.to_numpy(), "station_id": out["station_id"].astype(str).to_numpy()}
        )
        cap = pd.Series(
            left.merge(cmap, on=keys, how="left")["capacity"].to_numpy(), index=out.index
        )
    elif "capacity" in out.columns:
        cap = out["capacity"]

    if len(present) == 2 and cap is not None:
        b = pd.to_numeric(out[present[0]], errors="coerce")
        d = pd.to_numeric(out[present[1]], errors="coerce")
        c = pd.to_numeric(cap, errors="coerce")
        suspect = pd.Series(((b == 0) & (d == 0) & (c > 0)).to_numpy(), index=out.index).astype(
            "boolean"
        )
        suspect[(b.isna() | d.isna() | c.isna()).to_numpy()] = pd.NA
    else:
        suspect = pd.Series(pd.NA, index=out.index, dtype="boolean")

    out["field_unsupported_by_operator"] = flag_text.replace("", pd.NA).astype("string")
    out["both_zero_suspect"] = suspect
    out["network_all_zero_anomaly"] = anomaly
    return out

docs.title: release: freezing a period
docs.text:
Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules (2.1.0). See the overview.

freeze_release turns a closed UTC period of a lake into a new folder:

data/<table>/system_id=<id>/year=2026/month=03/data.parquet    cut at the period's bounds
daily_coverage.csv, daily_coverage.parquet                      polls expected and obtained per day
incidents.csv, incidents.json                                   the registry for the period
data_manifest.json                                              rows and content fingerprint
datapackage.json                                                Frictionless Data Package
croissant.json                                                  Croissant metadata (optional)
README.md                                                       what is in it, coverage, incidents, licence
SHA256SUMS                                                      one checksum per file

It uploads nothing and registers nothing. Depositing the folder (Zenodo, Dataverse, a bucket) is yours to do, and so is the choice of licence: there is no default. Without license= the README says the release has no licence declared. producers= lists who published the original feeds, to credit.

It refuses a period that is not over (allow_open_period=True overrides it) and a destination that is not empty: a release is written once.

The coverage and the incidents are computed from the released rows with quality, so the README states honestly which days are complete. The Croissant file is a minimal description (record set, fields, the Parquet file set); validate it with the MLCommons tools before relying on it.

docs.title: Verifying
docs.text: verify_release(folder) checks every file against SHA256SUMS (the file sha256sum -c reads) and refuses unlisted files; deep=True also reads the table back and compares it with data_manifest.json (rows and content fingerprint), which catches a file that was re-encoded and re-checksummed.

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from gbfs_toolkit.release import freeze_release, verify_release
from gbfs_toolkit.store import write_lake

t = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=2 * 1440, freq="min", tz="UTC")
snapshots = pd.concat([
    pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "alpha", "station_id": "s1", "observed_at_utc": t,
                  "num_bikes_available": 3, "num_docks_available": 5}),
    pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "beta", "station_id": "s1", "observed_at_utc": t[:1440],
                  "num_bikes_available": 3, "num_docks_available": 5}),     # silent on the 2nd
])
work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
write_lake(snapshots, work / "lake")

info = freeze_release(
    work / "lake", work / "release", name="demo-2026-03",
    start="2026-03-01", end="2026-03-02", license="CC-BY-4.0",
    producers=[{"system_id": "alpha", "producer": "City of Alpha", "license": "Open licence 2.0"}],
    incidents=[{"incident_id": "migration", "start_utc": "2026-03-01T00:00Z", "end_utc": "2026-03-01T06:00Z",
                "scope": "alpha", "cause": "ambiguous_missing_value", "summary": "Counts were written as 0 when missing."}],
)
print(info["rows"], info["systems"], info["files"])
print(sorted(p.name for p in (work / "release").iterdir()))
print((work / "release" / "README.md").read_text()[:900])

print(verify_release(work / "release", deep=True))
(work / "release" / "README.md").write_text("edited after the fact")
print(verify_release(work / "release", strict=False)["mismatched"])

docs.title: release
docs.text:
Freeze a closed period of a lake into a folder you can deposit anywhere.

Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules added in 2.1.0: names, parameters and output columns may change in a minor release (see the API policy).

freeze_release takes a lake written by gbfs_toolkit.store, a closed UTC period (it refuses a period that is not over) and some systems, and writes a new folder::

<out>/data/<table>/system_id=<id>/year=2026/month=03/data.parquet   cut at the period's bounds
<out>/daily_coverage.csv, daily_coverage.parquet                     polls expected and obtained per day
<out>/incidents.csv, incidents.json                                  the registry for the period
<out>/data_manifest.json                                             rows and content fingerprint
<out>/datapackage.json                                               Frictionless Data Package
<out>/croissant.json                                                 Croissant metadata (optional)
<out>/README.md                                                      what is in it, coverage, licence
<out>/SHA256SUMS                                                     one checksum per file

It uploads nothing and registers nothing: depositing the folder (Zenodo, Dataverse, a bucket) is yours to do, and so is the choice of licence. verify_release checks a folder against its SHA256SUMS (the same file sha256sum -c reads), which is what a downstream user runs.

The coverage and incidents come from gbfs_toolkit.quality, computed on the released rows, so the README states honestly which days are complete and which are not. The Croissant file is a minimal Croissant 1.0 description (record set, fields, the Parquet file set); the test suite validates it with the MLCommons mlcroissant package when that is installed. Needs pip install gbfs-toolkit[parquet].

Examples:

>>> import tempfile, pandas as pd
>>> from gbfs_toolkit.store import write_lake
>>> from gbfs_toolkit.release import freeze_release, verify_release
>>> t = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=1440, freq="min", tz="UTC")
>>> snaps = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "demo", "station_id": "s1", "observed_at_utc": t,
...                       "num_bikes_available": 3, "num_docks_available": 5})
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
...     _ = write_lake(snaps, tmp + "/lake")
...     info = freeze_release(tmp + "/lake", tmp + "/release", name="demo-2026-03-01",
...                           start="2026-03-01", end="2026-03-01", license="CC0-1.0")
...     report = verify_release(tmp + "/release")
>>> info["rows"], report["ok"]
(1440, True)

table_schema(df: DataFrame, *, extra_text: Sequence[str] = ()) -> dict[str, Any]

A Frictionless Table Schema (field names and types) for a frame.

Types are integer, number, boolean, datetime, date or string; an empty cell is a missing value (missingValues is [""]). extra_text names more string fields (the partition column, which lives in the folder name).

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> schema = table_schema(pd.DataFrame({"n": pd.array([1, None], dtype="Int64"), "s": ["a", "b"]}))
>>> [(f["name"], f["type"]) for f in schema["fields"]]
[('n', 'integer'), ('s', 'string')]

def table_schema(df: pd.DataFrame, *, extra_text: Sequence[str] = ()) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """A Frictionless *Table Schema* (field names and types) for a frame.

    Types are ``integer``, ``number``, ``boolean``, ``datetime``, ``date`` or ``string``; an
    empty cell is a missing value (``missingValues`` is ``[""]``). ``extra_text`` names more
    string fields (the partition column, which lives in the folder name).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> schema = table_schema(pd.DataFrame({"n": pd.array([1, None], dtype="Int64"), "s": ["a", "b"]}))
    >>> [(f["name"], f["type"]) for f in schema["fields"]]
    [('n', 'integer'), ('s', 'string')]
    """
    fields = []
    for name in df.columns:
        s = df[name]
        if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s.dtype):
            kind = "boolean"
        elif pd.api.types.is_integer_dtype(s.dtype):
            kind = "integer"
        elif pd.api.types.is_float_dtype(s.dtype):
            kind = "number"
        elif pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(s.dtype):
            kind = "datetime"
        else:
            kind = "string"
        fields.append({"name": str(name), "type": kind})
    have = {f["name"] for f in fields}
    fields += [{"name": n, "type": "string"} for n in extra_text if n not in have]
    return {"fields": fields, "missingValues": [""]}

def freeze_release(
    lake: str | Path,
    out_dir: str | Path,
    *,
    name: str,
    start: str | pd.Timestamp,
    end: str | pd.Timestamp,
    systems: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    table: str = "station_status",
    time_col: str | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    description: str | None = None,
    license: str | None = None,
    producers: Sequence[Mapping[str, str]] | None = None,
    incidents: Any = None,
    coverage_options: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    croissant: bool = True,
    version: str = "1.0.0",
    cite_as: str | None = None,
    allow_open_period: bool = False,
    today: dt.date | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Write a frozen release of ``lake`` for the UTC days ``start`` to ``end`` (both inclusive).

    Parameters
    ----------
    lake : path
        A `gbfs_toolkit.store` lake.
    out_dir : path
        The release folder. It must not exist or must be empty: a release is written once.
    name : str
        The release name and version (``demo-2026-03``).
    systems : sequence of str, optional
        Systems to include (default: all that have data in the period).
    table : str, default "station_status"
        The table's name in the folder layout and the metadata.
    time_col : str, optional
        The lake's time column (default: the one recorded in ``lake.json``).
    title, description : str, optional
        For the data package and the README.
    license : str, optional
        An SPDX-style identifier (``CC0-1.0``, ``CC-BY-4.0``, ``ODbL-1.0``, ``ODC-By-1.0``,
        ``etalab-2.0`` are known by name and link). Choose it yourself; there is no default. If
        omitted the README says the release has **no licence declared**.
    producers : sequence of dict, optional
        Who published the original feeds, to credit: dicts with ``system_id`` and any of
        ``producer``, ``license``, ``license_url``, ``source``. Listed in the README.
    incidents : registry, path or None
        Incidents you know of (see `gbfs_toolkit.quality`); the ones that overlap the
        period are kept, and those the data reveal (collection gaps, silent feeds) are added.
    coverage_options : mapping, optional
        Options of `gbfs_toolkit.quality.daily_coverage` (``expected_polls``,
        ``poll_resolution``, ``ok_threshold_pct``).
    croissant : bool, default True
        Also write ``croissant.json`` (Croissant 1.0).
    version : str, default "1.0.0"
        The dataset version written in ``croissant.json``, which asks for ``MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH``
        (the release ``name`` stays the identifier of the release).
    cite_as : str, optional
        How to cite the dataset, written as ``citeAs`` in ``croissant.json`` (Croissant
        recommends it; leave it out until you have a DOI or a reference).
    allow_open_period : bool, default False
        Allow ``end`` to be today or later. A period still being collected is not a release.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``path, name, rows, systems, files, period``.

    Raises
    ------
    GBFSValidationError
        For an open period, a non-empty ``out_dir``, or no data in the period.
    """
    require_pyarrow("freeze_release")
    from gbfs_toolkit.quality import (
        daily_coverage,
        detect_incidents,
        incidents_overlapping,
        write_incidents,
    )
    from gbfs_toolkit.repro import MANIFEST_FILE, create_manifest, write_manifest
    from gbfs_toolkit.store import list_partitions, read_lake, read_lake_metadata, write_lake

    lo = to_utc([start]).iloc[0].normalize()
    last_day = to_utc([end]).iloc[0].normalize()
    hi = last_day + pd.Timedelta(days=1)
    check(last_day >= lo, f"the period ends ({last_day.date()}) before it starts ({lo.date()})")
    now_day = today or dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).date()
    check(
        allow_open_period or last_day.date() < now_day,
        f"the period must be closed: it ends on {last_day.date()}, and today is {now_day} (UTC)",
    )
    out = Path(out_dir)
    check(
        not out.exists() or not any(out.iterdir()),
        f"{out} exists and is not empty; a release is written once, into a new folder",
    )
    meta = read_lake_metadata(lake)
    tcol = time_col or meta.get("time_column", "observed_at_utc")
    wanted = None if systems is None else {str(s) for s in systems}
    parts = list_partitions(lake)
    span = set(_month_span(lo, hi))
    parts = parts[
        [
            (wanted is None or s in wanted) and (y, m) in span
            for s, y, m in zip(parts["system_id"], parts["year"], parts["month"], strict=True)
        ]
    ]
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data_root = out / "data" / table
    rows_total = 0
    coverage_inputs: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    for system, year, month in zip(parts["system_id"], parts["year"], parts["month"], strict=True):
        part_lo = max(lo, pd.Timestamp(year=int(year), month=int(month), day=1, tz="UTC"))
        part_hi = min(
            hi,
            pd.Timestamp(
                year=int(year) + (month == 12), month=int(month) % 12 + 1, day=1, tz="UTC"
            ),
        )
        df = read_lake(lake, systems=[system], start=part_lo, end=part_hi, time_col=tcol)
        if df.empty:
            continue
        write_lake(df, data_root, mode="replace", time_col=tcol)
        rows_total += len(df)
        keep = [
            c
            for c in ("system_id", tcol, "num_bikes_available", "num_docks_available")
            if c in df.columns
        ]
        coverage_inputs.append(df[keep])
    check(rows_total > 0, "nothing to freeze: the lake has no rows for these systems and days")
    released_systems = sorted(
        {str(s) for s in parts["system_id"] if (data_root / f"system_id={s}").exists()}
    )
    snapshots = pd.concat(coverage_inputs, ignore_index=True)

    cov_opts = dict(coverage_options or {})
    coverage = daily_coverage(snapshots, time_col=tcol, start=lo, end=last_day, **cov_opts)
    known = incidents_overlapping(_incident_table(incidents), lo, hi, released_systems)
    registry = incidents_overlapping(
        detect_incidents(
            coverage,
            snapshots,
            known=known,
            time_col=tcol,
            min_collector_gap=cov_opts.get("min_collector_gap", "60min"),
        ),
        lo,
        hi,
        released_systems,
    )
    cov_out = coverage.copy()
    cov_out["date_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(cov_out["date_utc"])
    cov_out.to_csv(out / "daily_coverage.csv", index=False)
    cov_out.to_parquet(out / "daily_coverage.parquet", index=False, compression="zstd")
    write_incidents(registry, out / "incidents.json")
    write_incidents(registry, out / "incidents.csv")

    data_files = sorted(p.relative_to(out).as_posix() for p in data_root.rglob("*.parquet"))
    full = read_lake(data_root, time_col=tcol)
    manifest = create_manifest(
        full, table=table, systems=released_systems, start=lo, end=last_day, source=name
    )
    write_manifest(manifest, out / MANIFEST_FILE)
    schema = table_schema(full, extra_text=["system_id"])
    licenses = []
    if license:
        label, url = _LICENSES.get(license, (license, None))
        licenses = [{"name": license, "title": label, **({"path": url} if url else {})}]
    else:
        _log.warning("freeze_release: no licence declared; the README says so")
    created = pd.Timestamp.now(tz="UTC").strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    heading = title or f"GBFS {table.replace('_', ' ')}, {lo.date()} to {last_day.date()}"
    package = {
        "profile": "tabular-data-package",
        "name": _slug(name),
        "title": heading,
        "version": name,
        "created": created,
        "description": description
        or (
            f"Snapshots of {len(released_systems)} bike-share system(s) for the UTC days {lo.date()} "
            f"to {last_day.date()}, with their daily coverage and incidents. `system_id` is the "
            "name of the folder a file is in."
        ),
        **({"licenses": licenses} if licenses else {}),
        "resources": [
            {
                "name": table,
                "type": "table",
                "format": "parquet",
                "mediatype": "application/vnd.apache.parquet",
                "path": data_files,
                "schema": schema,
            },
            {
                "name": "daily-coverage",
                "type": "table",
                "format": "csv",
                "mediatype": "text/csv",
                "path": "daily_coverage.csv",
                "schema": table_schema(cov_out),
            },
            {
                "name": "incidents",
                "type": "table",
                "format": "json",
                "mediatype": "application/json",
                "path": "incidents.json",
            },
        ],
    }
    _write_json(out / "datapackage.json", package)
    if croissant:
        _write_json(
            out / "croissant.json",
            _croissant(
                package,
                table,
                schema,
                licenses,
                created,
                version,
                cite_as,
                _sha256(out / "daily_coverage.csv"),
            ),
        )
    (out / "README.md").write_text(
        _readme(
            heading,
            name,
            table,
            lo,
            last_day,
            released_systems,
            data_files,
            rows_total,
            coverage,
            registry,
            licenses,
            producers or [],
            croissant,
        ),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    _write_checksums(out)
    _log.info("release %s: %d rows, %d file(s) -> %s", name, rows_total, len(data_files), out)
    return {
        "path": out,
        "name": name,
        "rows": rows_total,
        "systems": released_systems,
        "files": len(data_files),
        "period": (str(lo.date()), str(last_day.date())),
    }

docs.text:
verify_release(directory: str | Path, *, strict: bool = True, deep: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]

Check a release folder against its SHA256SUMS.

Every listed file must exist with the recorded checksum, and no file may be present that is not listed. With deep=True the table is also read back and compared with data_manifest.json (rows and content fingerprint), which catches a file that was re-encoded without being altered.

Returns:

Type Description dict

ok (bool), checked (count), missing, mismatched and unlisted (lists of paths). With strict (the default) a problem raises GBFSValidationError naming them.

Examples:

>>> verify_release("/nonexistent")
Traceback (most recent call last):
GBFSValidationError: no SHA256SUMS in /nonexistent
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/release.py 
def verify_release(
    directory: str | Path, *, strict: bool = True, deep: bool = False
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Check a release folder against its ``SHA256SUMS``.

    Every listed file must exist with the recorded checksum, and no file may be present that is
    not listed. With ``deep=True`` the table is also read back and compared with
    ``data_manifest.json`` (rows and content fingerprint), which catches a file that was
    re-encoded without being altered.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``ok`` (bool), ``checked`` (count), ``missing``, ``mismatched`` and ``unlisted`` (lists
        of paths). With ``strict`` (the default) a problem raises ``GBFSValidationError`` naming
        them.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> verify_release("/nonexistent")  # doctest: +IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL
    Traceback (most recent call last):
    GBFSValidationError: no SHA256SUMS in /nonexistent
    """
    root = Path(directory)
    sums = root / CHECKSUM_FILE
    check(sums.is_file(), f"no {CHECKSUM_FILE} in {root}")
    listed: dict[str, str] = {}
    for n, line in enumerate(sums.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        m = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9a-f]{64})  (.+)", line)
        if m is None:
            raise GBFSValidationError(f"{sums}, line {n}: not a 'sha256  path' line")
        digest, rel = m.groups()
        if rel.startswith("/") or ".." in Path(rel).parts:
            raise GBFSValidationError(f"{sums}, line {n}: unsafe path {rel!r}")
        listed[rel] = digest
    missing = sorted(rel for rel in listed if not (root / rel).is_file())
    mismatched = sorted(
        rel for rel, d in listed.items() if rel not in missing and _sha256(root / rel) != d
    )
    present = {
        p.relative_to(root).as_posix()
        for p in root.rglob("*")
        if p.is_file() and p.name != CHECKSUM_FILE
    }
    unlisted = sorted(present - set(listed))
    problems = []
    if missing:
        problems.append(f"missing: {missing[:5]}")
    if mismatched:
        problems.append(f"changed: {mismatched[:5]}")
    if unlisted:
        problems.append(f"not in {CHECKSUM_FILE}: {unlisted[:5]}")
    report: dict[str, Any] = {
        "ok": not problems,
        "checked": len(listed) - len(missing),
        "missing": missing,
        "mismatched": mismatched,
        "unlisted": unlisted,
    }
    if deep and not problems and (root / "data_manifest.json").is_file():
        from gbfs_toolkit.repro import read_manifest, verify_manifest
        from gbfs_toolkit.store import read_lake

        manifest = read_manifest(root / "data_manifest.json")
        result = verify_manifest(
            manifest, read_lake(root / "data" / manifest["table"]), strict=False
        )
        report["deep"] = result
        if not all(result.values()):
            report["ok"] = False
            problems.append(f"content differs from data_manifest.json: {result}")
    if problems and strict:
        raise GBFSValidationError(
            f"{root} does not match its {CHECKSUM_FILE}: " + "; ".join(problems)
        )
    return report

docs.title: repro: manifest and fingerprint
docs.text:
Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules (2.1.0). See the overview.

An analysis that cites "the stations of one city in March" is reproducible only if someone can check that the table they rebuilt is the table the authors used. gbfs_toolkit.repro provides the pieces.

docs.title: The fingerprint
docs.text:
fingerprint(table) is a SHA-256 of a table's content. It does not depend on the order of the rows, on the file format, or on the tool that wrote the file:

  • columns are taken by name (sorted), and the names are part of the hash, so renaming a column changes it;
  • numbers are written with 12 significant digits, so 1 and 1.0, or a float that went through another tool, agree. Differences beyond the 12th digit are not detected, by design;
  • times are microseconds since 1970 UTC; booleans 0 and 1; an empty value ∅;
  • each row is hashed (MD5), the hashes are sorted, and the names plus the hashes are hashed again.

The same value can be computed in DuckDB, for a table t:

SELECT 'sha256:' || sha256('col_a|col_b' || chr(10) || coalesce(string_agg(h, '' ORDER BY h), ''))
FROM (SELECT md5(concat_ws('|',
        coalesce(CAST(epoch_us(CAST("col_a" AS TIMESTAMPTZ)) AS VARCHAR), '∅'),
        coalesce(printf('%.12g', CASE WHEN isnan(CAST("col_b" AS DOUBLE)) THEN NULL
                                       ELSE CAST("col_b" AS DOUBLE) END), '∅'))) AS h
      FROM t);

(columns in alphabetical order, one coalesce expression per column by type; the test suite checks that this agrees with fingerprint.)

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text: create_manifest records the table name, how it was selected (systems, UTC days, columns), the number of rows and the fingerprint in a small JSON file. Nothing in it depends on a machine or a user. verify_manifest compares data with it; materialize reads the selection again from a lake (or a release's data/<table> folder, or your own reader), verifies it, and keeps a Parquet copy in a cache folder that git ignores. export_sample writes a few stations of a table, a few megabytes, as a lake plus a manifest of its own, for a CI run that cannot hold the real data (point your code at the sample folder in CI, at the real lake elsewhere).

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from gbfs_toolkit.repro import (
    create_manifest, export_sample, fingerprint, materialize, verify_manifest, write_manifest)
from gbfs_toolkit.store import write_lake

rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
t = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=3 * 288, freq="5min", tz="UTC")
table = pd.DataFrame({
    "system_id": "harbor", "station_id": [f"s{i % 12}" for i in range(len(t))], "observed_at_utc": t,
    "num_bikes_available": rng.integers(0, 15, len(t)),
})
work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
write_lake(table, work / "lake")

# What the analysis used: March 1st, as a manifest.
used = table[table.observed_at_utc < "2026-03-02"]
manifest = create_manifest(used, table="station_status", systems=["harbor"], start="2026-03-01", end="2026-03-01")
write_manifest(manifest, work / "data_manifest.json")

# Somebody else rebuilds it from the lake, in another row order, and checks it.
path = materialize(manifest, work / "lake", cache_dir=work / "cache")
print(verify_manifest(manifest, pd.read_parquet(path).sample(frac=1, random_state=0)))
print(fingerprint(used) == fingerprint(used.iloc[::-1]))

# A small copy for continuous integration.
sample = export_sample(table, work / "sample", table="station_status", stations=3)
print(sample["stations"], sample["rows"])

docs.title: repro
docs.text:
A data manifest and a content fingerprint, so an analysis can prove which data it read.

Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules added in 2.1.0: names, parameters and output columns may change in a minor release (see the API policy).

An analysis that cites "the stations of one city in March" is only reproducible if someone can check that the table they rebuilt is the table the authors used. The pieces here:

fingerprint a SHA-256 of a table's content. It does not depend on the order of the rows, on the file format, or on the tool that wrote the file: columns are taken by name, numbers are written with 12 significant digits (so 1 and 1.0, or a float that went through another tool, agree; differences beyond the 12th digit are not detected, by design), times as microseconds since 1970 UTC, booleans as 0 and 1, an empty value as ∅; each row is hashed (MD5), the hashes are sorted, and the sorted column names followed by the hashes are hashed again (SHA-256), so renaming a column changes the fingerprint. create_manifest / write_manifest / read_manifest a small JSON file naming the table, the systems, the UTC days, the columns, the number of rows and the fingerprint; verify_manifest the check, raising gbfs_toolkit.core.errors.GBFSValidationError when rows or fingerprint differ; materialize read the data a manifest describes from a lake (gbfs_toolkit.store, a release's data/ folder, or your own reader), verify it, and keep a Parquet copy in a cache folder that git ignores; export_sample a few stations of a table, a few megabytes, for a continuous-integration run that cannot hold the real data.

The documentation page gives the equivalent DuckDB expression, so a table fingerprinted here and in SQL agree (a test checks it). Parquet needs pip install gbfs-toolkit[parquet].

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from gbfs_toolkit.repro import fingerprint
>>> a = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2], "t": pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-01", "2026-01-02"], utc=True)})
>>> b = a.iloc[::-1].assign(x=[2.0, 1.0])[["t", "x"]]
>>> fingerprint(a) == fingerprint(b)
True
>>> fingerprint(a).startswith("sha256:")
True

The content fingerprint "sha256:<hex>" of a table (see the module description).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data DataFrame, path, or lake folder

required exclude sequence of str

False
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/repro.py 
def fingerprint(data: Any, *, exclude: Sequence[str] = ()) -> str:
    """The content fingerprint ``"sha256:<hex>"`` of a table (see the module description).

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : DataFrame, path, or lake folder
        A frame, a Parquet file, a folder of Parquet files, or a `gbfs_toolkit.store` lake.
    exclude : sequence of str
        Columns to leave out (storage keys such as ``year`` and ``month``, say).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> fingerprint(pd.DataFrame({"a": []})) == fingerprint(pd.DataFrame({"b": []}))
    False
    """
    df = _load(data)
    names = sorted(str(c) for c in df.columns if str(c) not in set(exclude))
    if not names:
        return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(b"").hexdigest()
    by_name = {str(c): c for c in df.columns}
    parts = [_column_text(df[by_name[n]].reset_index(drop=True)) for n in names]
    rows = parts[0].str.cat(parts[1:], sep="|") if len(parts) > 1 else parts[0]
    hashes = sorted(hashlib.md5(r.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() for r in rows)
    header = "|".join(names) + "\n"
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256((header + "".join(hashes)).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

def create_manifest(
    data: Any,
    *,
    table: str,
    systems: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    start: str | pd.Timestamp | None = None,
    end: str | pd.Timestamp | None = None,
    columns: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    exclude: Sequence[str] = (),
    source: str | None = None,
    extra: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Describe ``data`` (what an analysis read) and fingerprint it.

    ``systems``, ``start`` and ``end`` (UTC days, both inclusive) and ``columns`` record how the
    table was selected, so `materialize` can select it again. ``source`` is free text: a
    release name, a lake path, a DOI. Nothing in the manifest depends on a machine or a user.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> m = create_manifest(pd.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3]}), table="demo", start="2026-01-01", end="2026-01-31")
    >>> m["rows"], m["start_utc"], m["format"]
    (3, '2026-01-01', 'gbfs-toolkit-data-manifest/1')
    """
    from gbfs_toolkit import __version__

    df = _load(data)
    manifest: dict[str, Any] = {
        "format": MANIFEST_FORMAT,
        "table": table,
        "systems": list(systems) if systems else None,
        "start_utc": _day(start),
        "end_utc": _day(end),
        "columns": list(columns) if columns else None,
        "exclude": list(exclude),
        "rows": int(len(df)),
        "fingerprint": fingerprint(df, exclude=exclude),
        "source": source,
        "toolkit_version": __version__,
        "created_at": pd.Timestamp.now(tz="UTC").strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    }
    if extra:
        manifest.update(extra)
    return manifest

def write_manifest(manifest: dict[str, Any], path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Write a manifest as indented JSON (atomically) and return its path."""
    out = Path(path)
    atomic_write(
        out,
        lambda tmp: tmp.write_text(
            json.dumps(manifest, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
        ),
    )
    return out

def read_manifest(path: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read a manifest file, checking that it is one.

    Raises
    ------
    GBFSValidationError
        If the file is not JSON, or carries another ``format`` or no ``table``.
    """
    try:
        manifest = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise GBFSValidationError(f"{path} is not a JSON manifest: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(manifest, dict) or manifest.get("format") != MANIFEST_FORMAT:
        raise GBFSValidationError(f"{path} is not a {MANIFEST_FORMAT} manifest")
    check(bool(manifest.get("table")), f"{path}: the manifest names no table")
    return manifest

def verify_manifest(manifest: dict[str, Any], data: Any, *, strict: bool = True) -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Compare ``data`` with what ``manifest`` recorded: the row count and the fingerprint.

    Returns ``{"rows": bool, "fingerprint": bool}``. With ``strict`` (the default) any
    difference raises ``GBFSValidationError`` whose message names both values.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> df = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2]})
    >>> m = create_manifest(df, table="t")
    >>> verify_manifest(m, df)
    {'rows': True, 'fingerprint': True}
    """
    df = _load(data)
    result = {"rows": True, "fingerprint": True}
    problems = []
    if manifest.get("rows") is not None and int(manifest["rows"]) != len(df):
        result["rows"] = False
        problems.append(f"{len(df)} rows instead of {manifest['rows']}")
    if manifest.get("fingerprint"):
        got = fingerprint(df, exclude=manifest.get("exclude") or ())
        if got != manifest["fingerprint"]:
            result["fingerprint"] = False
            problems.append(
                f"fingerprint {got[:19]}... instead of {manifest['fingerprint'][:19]}..."
            )
    if problems and strict:
        raise GBFSValidationError(
            f"the data differ from the manifest of {manifest.get('table')!r}: "
            + "; ".join(problems)
        )
    return result

def materialize(
    manifest: dict[str, Any] | str | Path,
    lake: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    cache_dir: str | Path,
    reader: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], pd.DataFrame] | None = None,
    verify: bool = True,
    load: bool = False,
) -> Path | pd.DataFrame:
    """Read the data a manifest describes, check it, and keep a Parquet copy in ``cache_dir``.

    The rows are read from ``lake`` (a `gbfs_toolkit.store` lake, such as a release's
    ``data/<table>`` folder) restricted to the manifest's systems, days and columns, or from
    ``reader(manifest)`` if you pass one. With ``verify`` the copy must match the manifest's
    rows and fingerprint, or ``GBFSValidationError`` is raised and nothing is kept. A later call
    with the same manifest returns the cached copy without reading the lake again. The cache
    folder gets a ``.gitignore`` that ignores everything in it.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path or pandas.DataFrame
        The cached Parquet file, or the frame with ``load=True``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If neither ``lake`` nor ``reader`` is given.
    """
    require_pyarrow("materialize")
    m = read_manifest(manifest) if isinstance(manifest, (str, Path)) else manifest
    if lake is None and reader is None:
        raise ValueError("materialize needs a lake folder or a reader")
    cache = Path(cache_dir)
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ignore = cache / ".gitignore"
    if not ignore.exists():
        ignore.write_text(
            "# cache of gbfs_toolkit.repro.materialize: keep it out of git\n*\n", encoding="utf-8"
        )
    name = f"{m['table']}-{_selection_key(m)}"
    path, witness = cache / f"{name}.parquet", cache / f"{name}.verified"
    wanted = m.get("fingerprint")
    if path.exists() and (
        not verify or not wanted or (witness.exists() and witness.read_text().strip() == wanted)
    ):
        return pd.read_parquet(path) if load else path
    if reader is not None:
        df = reader(m)
    else:
        from gbfs_toolkit.store import read_lake

        end = m.get("end_utc")
        df = read_lake(
            lake,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            systems=m.get("systems"),
            start=m.get("start_utc"),
            end=None if end is None else pd.Timestamp(end, tz="UTC") + pd.Timedelta(days=1),
            columns=m.get("columns"),
        )
    if verify:
        verify_manifest(m, df)
    atomic_write(path, lambda tmp: df.to_parquet(tmp, index=False, compression="zstd"))
    if wanted and verify:
        witness.write_text(wanted, encoding="utf-8")
    _log.info("materialized %s: %d rows -> %s", m["table"], len(df), path)
    return df if load else path
