def export_sample(
    data: Any,
    out_dir: str | Path,
    *,
    table: str,
    stations: int = 5,
    station_col: str = "station_id",
    max_bytes: int = 5_000_000,
    time_col: str | None = None,
    source: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """A small copy of a table for a CI run: ``stations`` stations, under ``max_bytes``.

    The first ``stations`` identifiers (sorted) are kept; the set is halved until the Parquet
    files fit in ``max_bytes``. The sample is written as a lake under
    ``<out_dir>/data/<table>/`` (so `materialize` and
    `gbfs_toolkit.store.read_lake` read it like the real one) next to a
    ``data_manifest.json`` that fingerprints the sample itself and lists its stations.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The manifest that was written.

    Raises
    ------
    GBFSValidationError
        If the table has no ``station_col`` column, or is empty.
    """
    from gbfs_toolkit.store import write_lake

    require_pyarrow("export_sample")
    df = _load(data)
    check(len(df) > 0, "export_sample: the table is empty")
    check(station_col in df.columns, f"export_sample: no {station_col!r} column to sample by")
    ids = sorted(df[station_col].astype(str).unique())
    keep = ids[: max(1, stations)]
    root = Path(out_dir)
    folder = root / "data" / table
    while True:
        if folder.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(folder)
        part = df[df[station_col].astype(str).isin(keep)]
        write_lake(part, folder, time_col=time_col)
        size = sum(f.stat().st_size for f in folder.rglob("*.parquet"))
        if size <= max_bytes or len(keep) <= 1:
            break
        keep = keep[: max(1, len(keep) // 2)]
    from gbfs_toolkit.store import read_lake

    sample = read_lake(folder)
    times = to_utc(
        part[time_col or ("observed_at_utc" if "observed_at_utc" in part else "fetched_at")]
    )
    manifest = create_manifest(
        sample,
        table=table,
        systems=sorted(part["system_id"].astype(str).unique())
        if "system_id" in part.columns
        else None,
        start=times.min(),
        end=times.max(),
        source=source,
        extra={"sample": True, "stations": keep, "bytes": int(size)},
    )
    write_manifest(manifest, root / MANIFEST_FILE)
    return manifest

docs.title: stations.match: following station identifiers
docs.text:
Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules (2.1.0). See the overview.

Operators renumber stations, re-issue ids when they change platform, and move a dock a few metres. A study that spans two periods needs to know which station of the first is which of the second. match_stations(old, new) pairs them one to one, within a system, in three passes, and labels each pair with the rule that made it:

match_method Rule same_id the identifier exists in both tables (and the stations are within same_id_far_m, 300 m) same_id_far same identifier, more than same_id_far_m apart: probably not the same place, check it same_name among what is left: equal normalised names (case, accents, punctuation and a leading "042 - " ignored) within name_radius_m (150 m) nearest among what is left: within radius_m (100 m), closest first none in old only: the station disappeared only_new in new only: it appeared

Keep the safe pairs (same_id, same_name) and look at the others. Two systems that reuse the same numbers never match each other, and ids stay text so a leading zero survives. id_continuity summarises, for consecutive periods, how much of the numbering survives.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import pandas as pd

from gbfs_toolkit.stations.match import id_continuity, match_stations

def stations(rows):
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["system_id", "station_id", "name", "lat", "lon"])

y2025 = stations([("harbor", "1", "Gare", 45.760, 4.860), ("harbor", "2", "Mairie", 45.770, 4.850),
                  ("harbor", "3", "Port", 45.780, 4.840), ("harbor", "4", "Parc", 45.790, 4.830)])
y2026 = stations([("harbor", "1", "Gare", 45.760, 4.860),            # same id
                  ("harbor", "20", "MAIRIE", 45.7701, 4.850),         # renumbered, same name
                  ("harbor", "44", "Jardin", 45.7901, 4.830),         # renumbered and renamed, 11 m away
                  ("harbor", "99", "Stade", 45.900, 4.800)])          # new

matches = match_stations(y2025, y2026)
print(matches[["station_id_old", "station_id_new", "match_method", "distance_m"]].to_string(index=False))
print(id_continuity({"2025": y2025, "2026": y2026})[["n_old", "n_same_id", "n_matched_other", "n_lost", "n_new_only"]])

docs.title: match
docs.text:
Follow stations from one period (or source) to the next when their identifiers change.

Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules added in 2.1.0: names, parameters and output columns may change in a minor release (see the API policy).

Operators renumber stations, re-issue identifiers when they change platform, and move a dock a few metres. A study that spans two periods needs to know which station of the first is which of the second. match_stations pairs them one to one, in three passes, and says which rule made each pair, so you can keep the safe pairs and look at the others:

  1. same_id: the identifier exists in both. If the two coordinates are more than same_id_far_m apart the pair is labelled same_id_far instead (same id, probably not the same place: check it).
  2. same_name: among what is left, the normalised names are equal (case, accents, punctuation and a leading "123 - " number are ignored) and the stations are within name_radius_m.
  3. nearest: among what is left, the stations within radius_m, closest first.

What remains is reported as none (in the old table only: the station disappeared) or only_new (in the new table only: it appeared). Matching is done system by system, so two systems that reuse the same numbers never match each other. The result is deterministic: ties are broken by distance and then by identifier.

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from gbfs_toolkit.stations.match import match_stations
>>> old = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["1", "2", "3"],
...                     "name": ["Gare", "Mairie", "Port"],
...                     "lat": [43.600, 43.610, 43.620], "lon": [3.88, 3.88, 3.88]})
>>> new = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["1", "20", "99"],
...                     "name": ["Gare", "MAIRIE", "Stade"],
...                     "lat": [43.600, 43.6101, 43.700], "lon": [3.88, 3.88, 3.88]})
>>> m = match_stations(old, new)
>>> m["match_method"].tolist()
['same_id', 'same_name', 'none', 'only_new']
>>> m["station_id_old"].fillna("-").tolist(), m["station_id_new"].fillna("-").tolist()
(['1', '2', '3', '-'], ['1', '20', '-', '99'])

def normalize_station_name(name: Any) -> str:
    """A name reduced to what identifies it: ASCII, upper case, letters and digits only.

    A leading station number (``"042 - "``, ``"12: "``) is dropped, because operators add and
    remove it.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> normalize_station_name("042 - Place de l'Europe") == normalize_station_name("PLACE DE L EUROPE")
    True
    >>> normalize_station_name("42 - Hôtel de Ville"), normalize_station_name(None)
    ('HOTELDEVILLE', '')
    """
    if name is None or (isinstance(name, float) and name != name) or name is pd.NA:
        return ""
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", str(name)).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode().upper()
    text = re.sub(r"^\s*\d+\s*[-–:]\s*", "", text)
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]", "", text)

) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Pair the stations of ``old`` with those of ``new``, one to one (see the module).

    Parameters
    ----------
    old, new : pandas.DataFrame
        ``station_id``; ``system_id`` (optional, matches are made within a system);
        ``name``, ``lat``, ``lon`` (optional: without coordinates only identical ids match).
    same_id_far_m : float, default 300
        Distance beyond which an identical id is labelled ``same_id_far``.
    name_radius_m : float, default 150
        Largest distance between two stations whose normalised names are equal.
    radius_m : float, default 100
        Largest distance between two stations matched on position alone.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `MATCH_COLUMNS`, one row per old station, per new station, or per pair, sorted
        by system then identifier. Ids are text, so a leading zero survives.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> a = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["a"], "lat": [43.0], "lon": [3.0]})
    >>> b = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["z"], "lat": [43.0005], "lon": [3.0]})
    >>> row = match_stations(a, b).iloc[0]
    >>> row["match_method"], round(float(row["distance_m"]))
    ('nearest', 56)
    """
    for name, value in (
        ("same_id_far_m", same_id_far_m),
        ("name_radius_m", name_radius_m),
        ("radius_m", radius_m),
    ):
        if value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must not be negative")
    a, b = _prepare(old, "match_stations(old)"), _prepare(new, "match_stations(new)")
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for system in sorted(set(a["system_id"]) | set(b["system_id"])):
        sub = _match_system(
            a[a["system_id"] == system].reset_index(drop=True),
            b[b["system_id"] == system].reset_index(drop=True),
            same_id_far_m,
            name_radius_m,
            radius_m,
        )
        rows += [{"system_id": system, **r} for r in sub]
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=MATCH_COLUMNS)
    for c in ("station_id_old", "station_id_new", "name_old", "name_new"):
        out[c] = out[c].astype("string")
    order = {m: k for k, m in enumerate(METHODS)}
    out = out.assign(
        _m=out["match_method"].map(order),
        _k=out["station_id_old"].fillna(out["station_id_new"]),
    ).sort_values(["system_id", "_m", "_k"], kind="stable")
    if "system_id" not in old.columns and "system_id" not in new.columns:
        out["system_id"] = None
    _log.info("matched %s", out["match_method"].value_counts().to_dict())
    return out.drop(columns=["_m", "_k"]).reset_index(drop=True)

docs.text:
id_continuity(periods: Mapping[str, DataFrame], **options: float) -> DataFrame

How much of the station numbering survives from each period to the next.

periods maps a label to the station table of that period, in chronological order (a dict keeps it). For each consecutive pair and each system the result counts the stations kept under the same id, found under another id or place, lost and appeared, and the median distance moved by those that matched. options go to match_stations.

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

from_period, to_period, system_id, n_old, n_new, n_same_id, n_matched_other, n_lost, n_new_only, share_same_id, median_distance_m.

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> t1 = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["a", "b"]})
>>> t2 = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["a", "c"]})
>>> r = id_continuity({"2025": t1, "2026": t2}).iloc[0]
>>> int(r["n_same_id"]), int(r["n_lost"]), float(r["share_same_id"])
(1, 1, 0.5)
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/stations/match.py 
def id_continuity(periods: Mapping[str, pd.DataFrame], **options: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """How much of the station numbering survives from each period to the next.

    ``periods`` maps a label to the station table of that period, in chronological order
    (a ``dict`` keeps it). For each consecutive pair and each system the result counts the
    stations kept under the same id, found under another id or place, lost and appeared, and
    the median distance moved by those that matched. ``options`` go to `match_stations`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        ``from_period, to_period, system_id, n_old, n_new, n_same_id, n_matched_other, n_lost,
        n_new_only, share_same_id, median_distance_m``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> t1 = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["a", "b"]})
    >>> t2 = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["a", "c"]})
    >>> r = id_continuity({"2025": t1, "2026": t2}).iloc[0]
    >>> int(r["n_same_id"]), int(r["n_lost"]), float(r["share_same_id"])
    (1, 1, 0.5)
    """
    labels = list(periods)
    rows = []
    for left, right in zip(labels[:-1], labels[1:], strict=True):
        m = match_stations(periods[left], periods[right], **options)
        for system, g in m.groupby("system_id", dropna=False, sort=True):
            method = g["match_method"]
            n_old = int(g["station_id_old"].notna().sum())
            same = int(method.isin(["same_id", "same_id_far"]).sum())
            matched = g[g["station_id_old"].notna() & g["station_id_new"].notna()]
            rows.append(
                {
                    "from_period": left,
                    "to_period": right,
                    "system_id": system,
                    "n_old": n_old,
                    "n_new": int(g["station_id_new"].notna().sum()),
                    "n_same_id": same,
                    "n_matched_other": int(method.isin(["same_name", "nearest"]).sum()),
                    "n_lost": int((method == "none").sum()),
                    "n_new_only": int((method == "only_new").sum()),
                    "share_same_id": same / n_old if n_old else float("nan"),
                    "median_distance_m": float(matched["distance_m"].median())
                    if len(matched)
                    else float("nan"),
                }
            )
    return pd.DataFrame(
        rows,
        columns=[
            "from_period",
            "to_period",
            "system_id",
            "n_old",
            "n_new",
            "n_same_id",
            "n_matched_other",
            "n_lost",
            "n_new_only",
            "share_same_id",
            "median_distance_m",
        ],
    )

docs.title: store: a Parquet lake
docs.text:
Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules (2.1.0). See the overview.

A lake is plain Hive-partitioned Parquet, which DuckDB, Arrow, Spark and pandas all read without this library:

<root>/system_id=<id>/year=2026/month=03/data.parquet
<root>/lake.json                                        # format, time column, time zones

The system is the folder name and is not repeated inside the files; a reader gets it back as the system_id column. Partitions follow the UTC year and month of the time column.

docs.title: Common columns
docs.text: harmonize gives station and vehicle snapshots the same names whoever collected them: fetched_at becomes observed_at_utc, last_reported becomes last_reported_utc, counts are nullable integers, flags nullable booleans, ids text. Given an IANA zone (tz=, or {system_id: zone}) it adds observed_at_local (the wall clock, no zone attached) and utc_offset_min, so the clock change is recorded rather than recomputed.

docs.title: Writing
docs.text:
mode A partition that already holds data "append" (default) a new part-<id>.parquet is added: nothing is lost, writers never touch the same file; duplicates are kept "merge" existing files and new rows are combined, exact duplicates dropped, one data.parquet remains "replace" the partition holds only the new rows

Files are written to a temporary name and renamed, so a reader never sees half a file.

write_lake takes a pandas frame, or, for volumes that do not fit in memory, an Arrow table or dataset, a DuckDB relation, or a path (a folder of Parquet files such as the day files of collect, a file, a glob, another lake). Those are written piece by piece: in "append" mode one UTC day at a time (a file per day and system), in the other two modes one (system, month) at a time, because merging or replacing needs the whole partition. The time column of such a source must be a timestamp.

docs.title: Reading
docs.text: read_lake(root, systems=..., start=..., end=..., columns=...) selects systems and the window start <= time < end (UTC), skipping the folders outside it before opening any file. output="arrow" returns a pyarrow.Table and output="duckdb" a lazy DuckDB relation over the selected files (nothing loaded). For a lake larger than memory, hand the folder itself to aggregate and quality: they read it in place.

docs.title: DuckDB views
docs.text: duckdb_view_sql returns a CREATE VIEW statement (no DuckDB needed to print it); register_duckdb_views runs it on a connection (extra duckdb). system_id is text, year and month integers, and a query that filters on them skips the other folders.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import tempfile

import pandas as pd

from gbfs_toolkit.store import (
    duckdb_view_sql, harmonize, list_partitions, read_lake, write_lake)

times = pd.date_range("2026-01-31T22:00Z", periods=240, freq="min")      # crosses a month end
raw = pd.concat([
    pd.DataFrame({"system_id": system, "station_id": "s1", "fetched_at": times,
                  "num_bikes_available": 4, "num_docks_available": 6})
    for system in ("007", "harbor")
])
root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
write_lake(harmonize(raw, tz={"007": "Europe/Paris", "harbor": "Europe/Paris"}), root)
print(list_partitions(root))

feb = read_lake(root, systems=["007"], start="2026-02-01")
print(len(feb), feb["system_id"].unique(), feb["observed_at_local"].min())   # "007" keeps its zeros

print(duckdb_view_sql(root, "station_status"))

import duckdb                                      # needs the duckdb extra
from gbfs_toolkit.store import register_duckdb_views

con = duckdb.connect()
register_duckdb_views(con, {"station_status": root})
print(con.sql("SELECT system_id, month, count(*) AS n FROM station_status GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL"))

docs.title: store
docs.text:
A Parquet lake partitioned by system, year and month, with common column names.

Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules added in 2.1.0: names, parameters and output columns may change in a minor release (see the API policy).

The layout is plain Hive partitioning, which DuckDB, Arrow, Spark and pandas all read without this library::

<root>/system_id=<id>/year=2026/month=03/data.parquet

harmonize gives station and vehicle snapshots the same column names whatever collected them (observed_at_utc, system_id, station_id ...), keeps time in UTC and, when you give the system's IANA time zone, adds the local wall clock and the UTC offset. write_lake writes a frame into the lake (never half-written files) and read_lake reads a system and a time window back, filtering on the partitions before it loads anything. register_duckdb_views exposes lakes as DuckDB views (extra duckdb).

Parquet needs pip install gbfs-toolkit[parquet]; the views need pip install gbfs-toolkit[duckdb].

Examples:

>>> import tempfile, pandas as pd
>>> from gbfs_toolkit.store import harmonize, write_lake, read_lake
>>> raw = pd.DataFrame({
...     "system_id": "demo", "station_id": ["s1", "s2"],
...     "fetched_at": pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01T10:00Z"] * 2),
...     "num_bikes_available": [3, 0], "num_docks_available": [7, 10]})
>>> tidy = harmonize(raw, tz="Europe/Paris")
>>> int(tidy.loc[0, "utc_offset_min"])
60
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as lake:
...     _ = write_lake(tidy, lake)
...     back = read_lake(lake, systems=["demo"])
>>> len(back), sorted(back["station_id"])
(2, ['s1', 's2'])

harmonize(df: DataFrame, kind: str = 'station_status', *, system_id: str | None = None, tz: str | Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> DataFrame

Common names and types for snapshots, with UTC time and, optionally, local time.

fetched_at becomes observed_at_utc and last_reported last_reported_utc, both tz-aware UTC; counts are nullable integers and flags nullable booleans, so a value the feed left out stays empty. system_id is filled from the argument when the frame lacks it. With tz (an IANA zone, or {system_id: zone}) the frame gains observed_at_local (the wall clock, no zone attached) and utc_offset_min.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kind ('station_status', 'vehicle_status')

Which fields lead the result; the other columns follow unchanged.

"station_status"

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For an unknown kind or a time zone that does not exist.

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> raw = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["s"], "fetched_at": ["2026-07-01T10:00:00Z"],
...                     "num_bikes_available": [2]})
>>> out = harmonize(raw, system_id="demo", tz="Europe/Paris")
>>> out.loc[0, "observed_at_local"].hour, int(out.loc[0, "utc_offset_min"])
(12, 120)
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/store.py 
def harmonize(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    kind: str = "station_status",
    *,
    system_id: str | None = None,
    tz: str | Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Common names and types for snapshots, with UTC time and, optionally, local time.

    ``fetched_at`` becomes ``observed_at_utc`` and ``last_reported`` ``last_reported_utc``, both
    tz-aware UTC; counts are nullable integers and flags nullable booleans, so a value the feed
    left out stays empty. ``system_id`` is filled from the argument when the frame lacks it.
    With ``tz`` (an IANA zone, or ``{system_id: zone}``) the frame gains ``observed_at_local``
    (the wall clock, no zone attached) and ``utc_offset_min``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    kind : {"station_status", "vehicle_status"}
        Which fields lead the result; the other columns follow unchanged.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For an unknown ``kind`` or a time zone that does not exist.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> raw = pd.DataFrame({"station_id": ["s"], "fetched_at": ["2026-07-01T10:00:00Z"],
    ...                     "num_bikes_available": [2]})
    >>> out = harmonize(raw, system_id="demo", tz="Europe/Paris")
    >>> out.loc[0, "observed_at_local"].hour, int(out.loc[0, "utc_offset_min"])
    (12, 120)
    """
    if kind not in ("station_status", "vehicle_status"):
        raise ValueError(f"kind must be 'station_status' or 'vehicle_status', got {kind!r}")
    out = df.rename(columns={k: v for k, v in _RENAMES.items() if k in df.columns}).copy()
    if "observed_at_utc" not in out.columns:
        need_columns(out, ["fetched_at"], what="harmonize")
    if "system_id" not in out.columns:
        if system_id is None:
            need_columns(out, ["system_id"], what="harmonize (or pass system_id=)")
        out["system_id"] = system_id
    out["system_id"] = out["system_id"].astype("string")
    out["observed_at_utc"] = to_utc(out["observed_at_utc"], what="observed_at_utc").to_numpy()
    if "last_reported_utc" in out.columns:
        out["last_reported_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(
            out["last_reported_utc"], utc=True, errors="coerce"
        )
    for c in _COUNTS:
        if c in out.columns:
            out[c] = pd.to_numeric(out[c], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
    for c in _FLAGS:
        if c in out.columns:
            out[c] = out[c].astype("boolean")
    for c in ("station_id", "vehicle_id"):
        if c in out.columns:
            out[c] = out[c].astype("string")
    if tz is not None:
        local, offset = [], []
        for obs, system in zip(out["observed_at_utc"], out["system_id"], strict=True):
            zone = _zone_of(tz, str(system))
            if zone is None:
                local.append(pd.NaT)
                offset.append(pd.NA)
                continue
            here = obs.tz_convert(zone)
            local.append(here.tz_localize(None))
            offset.append(int(here.utcoffset().total_seconds() // 60))
        out["observed_at_local"] = pd.to_datetime(local)
        out["utc_offset_min"] = pd.array(offset, dtype="Int16")
    lead = [c for c in STATION_STATUS_FIELDS if c in out.columns]
    return out[lead + [c for c in out.columns if c not in lead]]

docs.text:
write_lake(df: Any, root: str | Path, *, mode: str = 'append', time_col: str | None = None, timezones: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, compression: str = 'zstd') -> DataFrame

Write df into the lake under root, one partition per (system, UTC year, UTC month).

df is a pandas frame or, for volumes that do not fit in memory, an Arrow table or dataset, a DuckDB relation, or a path (a folder of Parquet files such as the day files of gbfs_toolkit.collect, a file, a glob, or another lake). Its time column must be a timestamp. A table, relation or path is written piece by piece: in "append" mode one UTC day at a time (one file per day and system, so the memory used is a day, not the source), in the other two modes one (system, month) at a time, because merging or replacing needs the whole partition.

mode says what happens to a partition that already holds data:

"append" (default) a new file part-<id>.parquet is added next to the others: nothing is lost, and concurrent writers never touch the same file. Duplicates are not removed; "merge" the partition's files and the new rows are combined, exact duplicate rows are dropped, and one data.parquet replaces them; "replace" the partition holds only the new rows.

The system is the folder name and is not repeated inside the files (a reader of the lake gets it back as the system_id column). Every file is written to a temporary name and renamed, so a reader never sees a half file. timezones ({system_id: zone}) is recorded in lake.json. The time column defaults to observed_at_utc (then fetched_at); it must be tz-aware or UTC-naive.

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

One row per touched partition: system_id, year, month, rows, path (the file, or the partition folder when a table was written in several files).

Examples:

>>> import tempfile, pandas as pd
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "a", "station_id": "s",
...                    "observed_at_utc": pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-31T23:59Z", "2026-02-01T00:01Z"])})
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as lake:
...     touched = write_lake(df, lake)
>>> touched[["year", "month", "rows"]].values.tolist()
[[2026, 1, 1], [2026, 2, 1]]
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/store.py 
def write_lake(
    df: Any,
    root: str | Path,
    *,
    mode: str = "append",
    time_col: str | None = None,
    timezones: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    compression: str = "zstd",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Write ``df`` into the lake under ``root``, one partition per (system, UTC year, UTC month).

    ``df`` is a pandas frame or, for volumes that do not fit in memory, an Arrow table or
    dataset, a DuckDB relation, or a path (a folder of Parquet files such as the day files of
    `gbfs_toolkit.collect`, a file, a glob, or another lake). Its time column must be a
    timestamp. A table, relation or path is written piece by piece: in ``"append"`` mode one UTC
    day at a time (one file per day and system, so the memory used is a day, not the source), in
    the other two modes one (system, month) at a time, because merging or replacing needs the
    whole partition.

    ``mode`` says what happens to a partition that already holds data:

    ``"append"`` (default)
        a new file ``part-<id>.parquet`` is added next to the others: nothing is lost, and
        concurrent writers never touch the same file. Duplicates are not removed;
    ``"merge"``
        the partition's files and the new rows are combined, exact duplicate rows are
        dropped, and one ``data.parquet`` replaces them;
    ``"replace"``
        the partition holds only the new rows.

    The system is the folder name and is not repeated inside the files (a reader of the lake
    gets it back as the ``system_id`` column). Every file is written to a temporary name and renamed, so a reader never sees a half
    file. ``timezones`` (``{system_id: zone}``) is recorded in ``lake.json``. The time column
    defaults to ``observed_at_utc`` (then ``fetched_at``); it must be tz-aware or UTC-naive.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per touched partition: ``system_id, year, month, rows, path`` (the file, or the
        partition folder when a table was written in several files).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import tempfile, pandas as pd
    >>> df = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "a", "station_id": "s",
    ...                    "observed_at_utc": pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-31T23:59Z", "2026-02-01T00:01Z"])})
    >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as lake:
    ...     touched = write_lake(df, lake)
    >>> touched[["year", "month", "rows"]].values.tolist()
    [[2026, 1, 1], [2026, 2, 1]]
    """
    if mode not in ("append", "merge", "replace"):
        raise ValueError(f"mode must be 'append', 'merge' or 'replace', got {mode!r}")
    require_pyarrow("write_lake")
    import pyarrow as pa

    table = open_table(df, what="write_lake")
    need_columns(pd.DataFrame(columns=table.columns()), ["system_id"], what="write_lake")
    tcol = _time_column(table.columns(), time_col)
    root_path = Path(root)
    summary: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    def record(sys_id: str, y: int, m: int, target: Path, rows: int) -> None:
        summary.append(
            {
                "system_id": sys_id,
                "year": y,
                "month": m,
                "rows": rows,
                "path": str(target.relative_to(root_path)),
            }
        )

    if is_pandas(df) or table.kind == "pandas":
        frame = df if is_pandas(df) else table.df  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        times = to_utc(frame[tcol], what=tcol)
        work = frame.copy()
        work[tcol] = times
        system = work["system_id"].astype(str)
        year, month = times.dt.year.to_numpy(), times.dt.month.to_numpy()
        groups = (
            pd.DataFrame({"s": system.to_numpy(), "y": year, "m": month})
            .groupby(["s", "y", "m"], sort=True)
            .groups
        )
        for (sys_id, y, m), idx in groups.items():
            part = work.iloc[np.asarray(idx)].drop(columns=["system_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)
            new = pa.Table.from_pandas(part, preserve_index=False)
            target, rows = _write_partition(
                root_path, str(sys_id), int(y), int(m), new, mode, compression
            )
            record(str(sys_id), int(y), int(m), target, rows)
        total = int(len(frame))
    else:
        total = 0
        span = table.time_range(tcol)
        for sys_id, y, m in _partitions_of(table, tcol) if span is not None else []:
            written: list[Path] = []
            rows_here = 0
            for lo, hi in _windows(mode, y, m, span):  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                part = _partition_rows(table, tcol, sys_id, lo, hi)
                if part.num_rows == 0:
                    continue
                hive = ("year", "month") if getattr(table, "lake", False) else ()
                part = part.drop_columns(
                    [c for c in ("system_id", *hive) if c in part.column_names]
                )
                idx = part.column_names.index(tcol)
                part = part.set_column(idx, tcol, _utc_arrow(part[tcol]))
                target, rows = _write_partition(root_path, sys_id, y, m, part, mode, compression)
                written.append(target)
                rows_here += rows
            if written:
                shown = written[0] if len(written) == 1 else written[0].parent
                record(sys_id, y, m, shown, rows_here)
                total += rows_here
    _update_metadata(root_path, tcol, timezones)
    _log.info("lake %s: %d row(s) in %d partition(s) (%s)", root_path, total, len(summary), mode)
    return pd.DataFrame(summary, columns=["system_id", "year", "month", "rows", "path"])

def list_partitions(root: str | Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The partitions present under ``root``: ``system_id, year, month, files, bytes``."""
    base = Path(root)
    rows = []
    for folder in sorted(base.glob("system_id=*/year=*/month=*")):
        files = list(folder.glob("*.parquet"))
        if not files:
            continue
        rows.append(
            {
                "system_id": folder.parent.parent.name.split("=", 1)[1],
                "year": int(folder.parent.name.split("=", 1)[1]),
                "month": int(folder.name.split("=", 1)[1]),
                "files": len(files),
                "bytes": sum(f.stat().st_size for f in files),
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["system_id", "year", "month", "files", "bytes"])

read_lake(root: str | Path, *, systems: Iterable[str] | None = None, start: str | Timestamp | None = None, end: str | Timestamp | None = None, columns: list[str] | None = None, time_col: str | None = None, output: str = 'pandas') -> Any

Read a lake back: systems and the window start <= time < end (UTC).

Systems and months outside the window are skipped from the folder names, before any file is opened. columns limits what is loaded (the partition folders year and month are returned only if you ask for them). An absent or empty lake returns an empty frame.

For a lake that does not fit in memory, pass the folder itself to those functions instead of reading it.

Raises:

Type Description GBFSValidationError

If root exists but has no recognisable partition and no readable file.

ValueError

For an unknown output.

Examples:

>>> import tempfile, pandas as pd
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": ["a", "b"], "station_id": "s",
...                    "observed_at_utc": pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01T10:00Z"] * 2)})
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as lake:
...     _ = write_lake(df, lake)
...     only_b = read_lake(lake, systems=["b"])
>>> only_b["system_id"].tolist()

def read_lake(
    root: str | Path,
    *,
    systems: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    start: str | pd.Timestamp | None = None,
    end: str | pd.Timestamp | None = None,
    columns: list[str] | None = None,
    time_col: str | None = None,
    output: str = "pandas",
) -> Any:
    """Read a lake back: ``systems`` and the window ``start <= time < end`` (UTC).

    Systems and months outside the window are skipped from the folder names, before any file
    is opened. ``columns`` limits what is loaded (the partition folders ``year`` and ``month``
    are returned only if you ask for them). An absent or empty lake returns an empty frame.

    ``output`` chooses what comes back: ``"pandas"`` (a frame, the default), ``"arrow"`` (a
    ``pyarrow.Table``, without the pandas copy) or ``"duckdb"`` (a lazy DuckDB relation over the
    selected files, nothing loaded: query it, or pass it to `gbfs_toolkit.aggregate` and
    `gbfs_toolkit.quality`). For a lake that does not fit in memory, pass the folder itself to
    those functions instead of reading it.

    Raises
    ------
    GBFSValidationError
        If ``root`` exists but has no recognisable partition and no readable file.
    ValueError
        For an unknown ``output``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import tempfile, pandas as pd
    >>> df = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": ["a", "b"], "station_id": "s",
    ...                    "observed_at_utc": pd.to_datetime(["2026-03-01T10:00Z"] * 2)})
    >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as lake:
    ...     _ = write_lake(df, lake)
    ...     only_b = read_lake(lake, systems=["b"])
    >>> only_b["system_id"].tolist()
    ['b']
    """
    if output not in ("pandas", "arrow", "duckdb"):
        raise ValueError(f"output must be 'pandas', 'arrow' or 'duckdb', got {output!r}")
    require_pyarrow("read_lake")
    import pyarrow as pa
    import pyarrow.compute as pc
    import pyarrow.dataset as ds

    base = Path(root)
    meta = read_lake_metadata(base)
    tcol = time_col or meta.get("time_column", "observed_at_utc")
    if not base.is_dir() or not any(base.glob("system_id=*/year=*/month=*/*.parquet")):
        if base.is_dir() and any(base.rglob("*.parquet")):
            raise GBFSValidationError(
                f"{base} has Parquet files but not the system_id=/year=/month= layout"
            )
        if output == "arrow":
            return pa.table({c: pa.array([], pa.null()) for c in (columns or [])})
        if output == "duckdb":
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"no Parquet file under {base}")
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=columns or [])
    files = sorted(str(f) for f in base.glob("system_id=*/year=*/month=*/*.parquet"))
    lo = None if start is None else to_utc([start]).iloc[0]
    hi = None if end is None else to_utc([end]).iloc[0]
    if output == "duckdb":
        rel = _PathTable(files, lake=True, root=str(base)).relation()
        conds = []
        if systems is not None:
            names = ", ".join(sql_text(str(x)) for x in systems) or "NULL"
            conds.append(f"{sql_name('system_id')} IN ({names})")
        c = f"(epoch_ns({sql_name(tcol)}) // 1000)"
        if lo is not None:
            conds.append(f"{c} >= {int(lo.value // 1000)}")
        if hi is not None:
            conds.append(f"{c} < {int(hi.value // 1000)}")
        if conds:
            rel = rel.filter(" AND ".join(conds))
        cols = (
            columns
            if columns is not None
            else [n for n in rel.columns if n not in ("year", "month")]
        )
        return rel.project(", ".join(sql_name(x) for x in cols))
    dataset = ds.dataset(
        files, format="parquet", partitioning=_partitioning(), partition_base_dir=str(base)
    )
    expr = None

    def both(a: Any, b: Any) -> Any:
        return b if a is None else a & b

    if systems is not None:
        expr = both(expr, ds.field("system_id").isin([str(s) for s in systems]))
    if lo is not None:
        ym = lo.year * 100 + lo.month
        expr = both(expr, (ds.field("year") * 100 + ds.field("month")) >= ym)
    if hi is not None:
        last = hi - pd.Timedelta(1, "ns")
        ym = last.year * 100 + last.month
        expr = both(expr, (ds.field("year") * 100 + ds.field("month")) <= ym)
    wanted = columns
    if columns is not None and (lo is not None or hi is not None) and tcol not in columns:
        wanted = [*columns, tcol]
    table = dataset.to_table(columns=wanted, filter=expr)
    if output == "arrow":
        if (lo is not None or hi is not None) and tcol in table.column_names:
            t = _utc_arrow(table[tcol])
            keep = pc.is_valid(t)
            if lo is not None:
                keep = pc.and_(keep, pc.greater_equal(t, pa.scalar(lo.to_pydatetime(), t.type)))
            if hi is not None:
                keep = pc.and_(keep, pc.less(t, pa.scalar(hi.to_pydatetime(), t.type)))
            table = table.filter(keep)
        drop = [] if columns is not None else ["year", "month"]
        keep_cols = [c for c in (columns or table.column_names) if c in table.column_names]
        return table.select([c for c in keep_cols if c not in drop])
    out = table.to_pandas()
    if (lo is not None or hi is not None) and tcol in out.columns:
        t = to_utc(out[tcol], what=tcol)
        mask = pd.Series(True, index=out.index)
        if lo is not None:
            mask &= t >= lo
        if hi is not None:
            mask &= t < hi
        out = out[mask.to_numpy()]
    if columns is not None:
        out = out[[c for c in columns if c in out.columns]]
    else:  # year and month are the time column's folders, not data
        out = out.drop(columns=[c for c in ("year", "month") if c in out.columns])
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

duckdb_view_sql(root: str | Path, name: str) -> str

The CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW statement that exposes a lake to DuckDB.

The view reads every Parquet file under root with Hive partitioning, so system_id, year and month are columns (typed text and integers) and queries on them skip the folders they exclude. It needs no import of DuckDB, so it can be printed and run elsewhere.

Examples:

>>> sql = duckdb_view_sql("/data/lake", "station_status")
>>> sql.startswith("CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW station_status AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet(")
True
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/store.py 
def duckdb_view_sql(root: str | Path, name: str) -> str:
    """The ``CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`` statement that exposes a lake to DuckDB.

    The view reads every Parquet file under ``root`` with Hive partitioning, so ``system_id``,
    ``year`` and ``month`` are columns (typed text and integers) and queries on them skip the
    folders they exclude. It needs no import of DuckDB, so it can be printed and run elsewhere.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sql = duckdb_view_sql("/data/lake", "station_status")
    >>> sql.startswith("CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW station_status AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet(")
    True
    """
    if not _IDENT.match(name):
        raise ValueError(f"view name {name!r} is not a plain SQL identifier")
    path = str(Path(root).resolve()).replace("'", "''")
    return (
        f"CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {name} AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{path}/*/*/*/*.parquet', "
        "hive_partitioning = true, union_by_name = true, "
        "hive_types = {'system_id': VARCHAR, 'year': INTEGER, 'month': INTEGER})"
    )

def register_duckdb_views(con: Any, tables: Mapping[str, str | Path]) -> list[str]:
    """Create one DuckDB view per lake: ``tables`` maps a view name to a lake folder.

    ``con`` is a ``duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection``. Returns the names created. Requires
    ``pip install gbfs-toolkit[duckdb]`` only to obtain the connection: the function just runs
    `duckdb_view_sql`.

    """
    created = []
    for name, root in tables.items():
        con.execute(duckdb_view_sql(root, name))
        created.append(name)
    return created

docs.title: trips: published trip files
docs.text:
Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules (2.1.0). See the overview.

Several operators publish one row per trip as open data, each in its own shape. gbfs_toolkit.trips reads these families into one table, TRIP_COLUMNS:

Format Operators Files lyft Lyft / Motivate: Citi Bike, Divvy, Bluebikes, Bay Wheels, Capital Bikeshare, Nice Ride... the current files (ride_id, started_at, ...) and the older ones (tripduration, starttime, ...; trip_id, from_station_id, ...; Start date, Start station number, ...) urban_sharing Urban Sharing: Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim ISO 8601 times with an offset, coordinates inline bts Bicycle Transit Systems: Indego, Metro Bike Share the published duration changes unit between years, so it is recomputed from the two times velomagg Vélomagg (Montpellier Méditerranée Métropole, open data under the ODbL) Departure, Return, Departure station, Return station, Covered distance (m), Duration (sec.), Manager, ...: local times, the station number in front of the name, text that may be double-encoded

ride_id is the operator's own trip identifier, never a user's.

Formats not covered

A format is added only when its columns have been checked against a real file; none is guessed, because a guessed reader would silently mislabel data. If you have another one, describe its columns once with TripFormat (below), and consider contributing it with a sample file.

docs.title: Vélomagg
docs.text:
The Montpellier file publishes one row per trip, with the local time and the operator's station numbers. read_trips(path, tz="Europe/Paris") gives:

  • start_station_id / start_station_name from "002 Comédie" (the number, then the name; a station with no number keeps its name and has an empty id), the same for the return;
  • text repaired when the file is UTF-8 read as Latin-1 and encoded again (ComÃ©die becomes Comédie; a value that is already right is left alone);
  • distance_m from Covered distance (m) and duration_s from Duration (sec.), as published (the duration is not recomputed from the two times: it differs by a few seconds from them);
  • ended_at empty when the file has no return time (a trip still open when the file was cut);
  • is_operator_staff, a nullable boolean carried from the Manager column: True where the operator marks the trip as made by its own staff, False where it does not, empty where the file is empty. The flag is the publisher's, carried as published; this module does nothing else with it. The other formats leave it empty.

The account column is never read

The file has an account number (new_account) that tells two trips of one person apart, and a bike number. Neither is carried over, and there is no option to keep them: a column that is not in the format cannot appear in the result. A test checks that no value of the account column reaches the output, whichever reader or format is used. Times and stations can still identify a person when combined, so read the licence and the publisher's terms before releasing anything made from the file.

docs.title: Time zones are explicit
docs.text: Most files publish local wall-clock times without a zone, so tz= (an IANA name such as "America/Chicago") is required for them; there is no default, because UTC would be a silent mistake. Times come out tz-aware UTC. A local time that does not exist (the hour skipped in spring) is moved to the first instant after the change, and one that happens twice (the repeated hour in autumn) is read as the second, standard-time occurrence. Both are flagged in started_at_tz_flag and ended_at_tz_flag ("nonexistent", "ambiguous"), never fixed silently.

docs.title: No personal data
docs.text: Birth year, gender, bike number and account number are dropped, and the schema has no user identifier. member_type is only member or casual.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import io

import pandas as pd

from gbfs_toolkit.trips import TripFormat, detect_format, normalize_trips, read_trips

current = (
    "ride_id,rideable_type,started_at,ended_at,start_station_id,end_station_id,member_casual\n"
    "r1,electric_bike,2024-03-10 01:50:00,2024-03-10 03:10:00,S1,S2,member\n"      # across the spring change
    "r2,classic_bike,2024-11-03 01:30:00,2024-11-03 01:45:00,S2,,casual\n"          # in the repeated hour
)
trips = read_trips(io.BytesIO(current.encode()), tz="America/New_York", network="demo")
print(trips[["ride_id", "started_at", "duration_s", "started_at_tz_flag", "end_station_id"]])

legacy = pd.DataFrame({"tripduration": [600], "starttime": ["2019-06-01 07:00:00"],
                       "stoptime": ["2019-06-01 07:10:00"], "usertype": ["Subscriber"],
                       "birth year": [1980], "gender": [1], "bikeid": [7]})
assert detect_format(legacy.columns) == "lyft"
print(normalize_trips(legacy, tz="America/New_York").columns.tolist())   # no personal fields

# A format of your own: describe the columns once.
mine = TripFormat("mycity", {"ride_id": ["id"], "started_at": ["debut"], "ended_at": ["fin"]},
                  times_have_offset=True)
raw = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1], "debut": ["2025-01-01T10:00:00+01:00"], "fin": ["2025-01-01T10:05:00+01:00"]})
print(normalize_trips(raw, mine)[["started_at", "duration_s"]])

# Vélomagg: two invented rows in the published shape (the account column is in the file, not in the result)
velomagg = (
    "Departure,Return,Bike,Departure station,Return station,Covered distance (m),Duration (sec.),"
    "Manager,new_account\n"
    "2025-03-29 23:55:38,2025-03-30 00:12:27,230,001 Place Exemple,002 CafÃ© de la Gare,2909,1001,False,900001\n"
    "2025-06-01 08:00:00,2025-06-01 08:10:00,619,001 Place Exemple,001 Place Exemple,0,600,True,900002\n"
)
ride = read_trips(io.BytesIO(velomagg.encode("utf-8")), tz="Europe/Paris", network="velomagg")
print(ride[["start_station_id", "end_station_name", "distance_m", "is_operator_staff"]])
assert "new_account" not in ride.columns and "900001" not in ride.astype(str).to_csv()

Large files: iter_trips(path, tz=..., chunksize=500_000) yields normalised chunks, and a .zip (nested zips included) is read member by member.

docs.title: trips
docs.text:
Readers for the trip files that operators publish, into one common schema.

Experimental

Part of the experimental data-lake modules added in 2.1.0: names, parameters and output columns may change in a minor release (see the API policy).

Several operators publish one row per trip as open data, each in its own shape. This module reads the families below into the same table, TRIP_COLUMNS:

lyft the Lyft / Motivate family (Citi Bike, Divvy, Bluebikes, Bay Wheels, Capital Bikeshare, Nice Ride...): the current files (ride_id, started_at, ended_at, start_station_id, start_lat ...) and the older ones (tripduration, starttime, stoptime, start station id ...; trip_id, from_station_id ...; Start date, Start station number ...); urban_sharing the Urban Sharing platform's files (Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim): ISO 8601 times with an offset, coordinates inline; bts the Bicycle Transit Systems files (Indego, Metro Bike Share); velomagg the open-data trip file of the Vélomagg bike share (Montpellier Méditerranée Métropole, ODbL; Departure, Return, Departure station ... with a three-digit station number in front of each name). Times are local (tz="Europe/Paris"), the file's text may be double-encoded (ComÃ©die) and is repaired, the station number becomes the station id, Covered distance (m) becomes distance_m, and the Manager column, which marks the operator's own staff, becomes the boolean is_operator_staff.

Anything else: describe the columns once with TripFormat and pass it as fmt. No format is guessed beyond these; in particular the module reads no format it has not been shown.

Time zones are explicit. Most files publish local wall-clock times without a zone, so tz (an IANA name such as "America/Chicago") is required for them: there is no default, because UTC would be a silent mistake. Times come out tz-aware UTC. A local time that does not exist (the hour skipped in spring) is moved to the first instant after the change and one that happens twice (the repeated hour in autumn) is read as the second, standard-time occurrence; both are flagged in started_at_tz_flag / ended_at_tz_flag ("nonexistent", "ambiguous"), never guessed silently.

No personal data is carried over. Birth year, gender and bike number are dropped, and the common schema has no user identifier; member_type is only member or casual. A column that is not in the format is never read into the result, so the account number of the Vélomagg file (new_account), which tells that two trips are by the same person, cannot come out, and there is no option to keep it. is_operator_staff says whether the operator marked the trip as made by its staff: it is the publisher's own flag, carried as published, and this module does nothing with it.

Examples:

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from gbfs_toolkit.trips import normalize_trips
>>> raw = pd.DataFrame({
...     "ride_id": ["r1"], "rideable_type": ["electric_bike"], "member_casual": ["member"],
...     "started_at": ["2025-07-04 08:00:00"], "ended_at": ["2025-07-04 08:12:30"],
...     "start_station_id": ["S1"], "end_station_id": ["S2"]})
>>> out = normalize_trips(raw, tz="America/New_York", network="demo")
>>> str(out.loc[0, "started_at"]), float(out.loc[0, "duration_s"])
('2025-07-04 12:00:00+00:00', 750.0)

The name of the FORMATS entry whose columns these are, or None.

>>> detect_format(["started_at", "ended_at", "duration", "start_station_latitude"])

def detect_format(columns: Sequence[str]) -> str | None:
    """The name of the `FORMATS` entry whose columns these are, or ``None``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> detect_format(["ride_id", "started_at", "ended_at", "start_lat", "start_lng"])
    'lyft'
    >>> detect_format(["started_at", "ended_at", "duration", "start_station_latitude"])
    'urban_sharing'
    >>> detect_format(["trip_id", "start_time", "end_time", "start_lon", "passholder_type"])
    'bts'
    >>> detect_format(["Departure", "Return", "Departure station", "Return station"])
    'velomagg'
    >>> detect_format(["a", "b"]) is None
    True
    """
    low = {str(c).lstrip("\ufeff").lower().strip() for c in columns}
    if {"departure", "return", "departure station", "return station"} <= low:
        return "velomagg"
    if {"started_at", "start_station_latitude"} <= low:
        return "urban_sharing"
    if "start_lon" in low and "start_time" in low:
        return "bts"
    lyft = FORMATS["lyft"]
    has_start = any(a.lower() in low for a in lyft.columns["started_at"])
    has_end = any(a.lower() in low for a in lyft.columns["ended_at"])
    return "lyft" if has_start and has_end else None

    ----------
    df : pandas.DataFrame
        The file as read (any dtypes; ``dtype=str`` is the safest way to read it).
    fmt : str or TripFormat, default "auto"
        A key of `FORMATS`, a `TripFormat`, or ``"auto"`` to use
        `detect_format`.
    tz : str, optional
        IANA zone of the file's local times. Required unless the format's times carry an offset.
    network, source_file : str, optional
        Written into the output columns of the same name.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Rows without a start time are dropped (and counted in the log); nothing else is. A value
        the file does not carry is empty (``<NA>``/``NaN``), not guessed.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For an unknown or undetectable format, or a missing ``tz``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandas as pd
    >>> raw = pd.DataFrame({"tripduration": [600], "starttime": ["2020-03-08 02:30:00"],
    ...                     "stoptime": ["2020-03-08 03:10:00"], "usertype": ["Subscriber"],
    ...                     "birth year": [1980], "gender": [1], "bikeid": [7]})
    >>> out = normalize_trips(raw, tz="America/New_York")
    >>> out.loc[0, "started_at_tz_flag"], out.loc[0, "member_type"], "gender" in out.columns
    ('nonexistent', 'member', False)
    """
    if isinstance(fmt, str):
        name = detect_format(list(df.columns)) if fmt == "auto" else fmt
        if name is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cannot tell the trip format from the columns {list(df.columns)[:8]}; "
                "pass fmt= (a key of FORMATS or a TripFormat)"
            )
        if name not in FORMATS:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown trip format {name!r}; known: {sorted(FORMATS)}")
        spec = FORMATS[name]
    else:
        spec = fmt
    if not spec.times_have_offset and tz is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"format {spec.name!r} publishes local times without a zone: pass tz='Area/City' "
            "(for instance tz='America/Chicago')"
        )
    lower = _lookup(df)
    cols = _present(spec, lower)
    for required in ("started_at", "ended_at"):
        if required not in cols:
            raise ValueError(
                f"format {spec.name!r}: no column for {required} in {list(df.columns)[:10]}"
            )

    out = pd.DataFrame(index=df.index)
    for common in TRIP_COLUMNS:
        if common in cols and common not in ("started_at", "ended_at", "is_operator_staff"):
            out[common] = df[cols[common]]
    if spec.split_station:
        for side in ("start", "end"):
            ids, names = f"{side}_station_id", f"{side}_station_name"
            if ids in out or names in out:
                source = out[names] if names in out else out[ids]
                out[ids], out[names] = _split_station(source)
    if spec.repair_text:
        for common in _TEXT:
            if common in out:
                out[common] = _repair_text(out[common])
    for common in _TEXT:
        out[common] = (
            _id_text(out[common])
            if common in out
            else pd.Series(pd.NA, index=df.index, dtype="string")
        )
    for common in _COORDS:
        out[common] = (
            pd.to_numeric(out[common], errors="coerce").astype("float64")
            if common in out
            else pd.Series(np.nan, index=df.index, dtype="float64")
        )

    raw_t = {
        k: pd.to_datetime(df[cols[k]], errors="coerce", format="mixed", utc=spec.times_have_offset)
        for k in ("started_at", "ended_at")
    }
    if spec.times_have_offset:
        started, ended = raw_t["started_at"], raw_t["ended_at"]
        flag_s = flag_e = pd.Series(pd.NA, index=df.index, dtype="string")
    else:
        assert tz is not None
        started, flag_s = _localize(_strip_offset_naive(raw_t["started_at"]), tz)
        ended, flag_e = _localize(_strip_offset_naive(raw_t["ended_at"]), tz)
    out["started_at"], out["ended_at"] = started, ended
    out["started_at_tz_flag"], out["ended_at_tz_flag"] = flag_s, flag_e

    computed = (ended - started).dt.total_seconds()
    published = next((lower[a.lower()] for a in spec.duration_alias if a.lower() in lower), None)
    if published is not None and not spec.recompute_duration:
        seconds = pd.to_numeric(df[published], errors="coerce") * spec.duration_scale
        out["duration_s"] = seconds.where(seconds.notna(), computed).astype("float64")
    else:
        out["duration_s"] = computed.astype("float64")

    out["is_operator_staff"] = (
        _as_flag(df[cols["is_operator_staff"]])
        if "is_operator_staff" in cols
        else pd.Series(pd.NA, index=df.index, dtype="boolean")
    )
    if "member_type" in cols:
        raw_member = df[cols["member_type"]]
        if spec.member_rule is not None:
            member = raw_member.map(spec.member_rule)
        else:
            low = raw_member.astype("string").str.lower().str.strip()
            member = low.map(dict(spec.member_map)).fillna(low) if spec.member_map else low
        out["member_type"] = member.astype("string")
    if "rideable_type" in cols and spec.rideable_map:
        low = out["rideable_type"].str.lower().str.strip()
        out["rideable_type"] = low.map(dict(spec.rideable_map)).fillna(low).astype("string")

    out["network"] = pd.Series(network, index=df.index, dtype="string")
    out["source_file"] = pd.Series(source_file, index=df.index, dtype="string")
    dropped = int(out["started_at"].isna().sum())
    if dropped:
        _log.warning("%d row(s) without a readable start time were dropped", dropped)
    return out.loc[out["started_at"].notna(), TRIP_COLUMNS].reset_index(drop=True)

Read a trip CSV (or a zip of CSVs, nested zips included) chunk by chunk, normalised.

Memory stays bounded by chunksize rows, which matters for a year of a large system. source_file records the file (archive.zip::inner.csv inside a zip). Arguments are those of normalize_trips.

Examples:

>>> import io
>>> csv = io.BytesIO(b"ride_id,started_at,ended_at\nr1,2025-01-01 10:00:00,2025-01-01 10:05:00\n")
>>> [len(c) for c in iter_trips(csv, tz="UTC", network="demo")]
[1]
Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/trips.py 
def iter_trips(
    path: str | Path | Any,
    fmt: str | TripFormat = "auto",
    *,
    tz: str | None = None,
    network: str | None = None,
    chunksize: int = 500_000,
) -> Iterator[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Read a trip CSV (or a zip of CSVs, nested zips included) chunk by chunk, normalised.

    Memory stays bounded by ``chunksize`` rows, which matters for a year of a large system.
    ``source_file`` records the file (``archive.zip::inner.csv`` inside a zip). Arguments are
    those of `normalize_trips`.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import io
    >>> csv = io.BytesIO(b"ride_id,started_at,ended_at\\nr1,2025-01-01 10:00:00,2025-01-01 10:05:00\\n")
    >>> [len(c) for c in iter_trips(csv, tz="UTC", network="demo")]
    [1]
    """
    for label, chunk in _csv_chunks(path, "<stream>", chunksize):
        yield normalize_trips(chunk, fmt, tz=tz, network=network, source_file=label)

Examples:

...                  b"1,2025-01-01 10:00:00,2025-01-01 10:05:00,39.9,-75.1,Walk-up\n")
>>> trips = read_trips(csv, tz="America/New_York")

Source code in src/gbfs_toolkit/trips.py 
def read_trips(
    path: str | Path | Any,
    fmt: str | TripFormat = "auto",
    *,
    tz: str | None = None,
    network: str | None = None,
    chunksize: int = 500_000,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """All the trips of a CSV or zip file as one frame (see `iter_trips` for huge files).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import io
    >>> csv = io.BytesIO(b"trip_id,start_time,end_time,start_lat,start_lon,passholder_type\\n"
    ...                  b"1,2025-01-01 10:00:00,2025-01-01 10:05:00,39.9,-75.1,Walk-up\\n")
    >>> trips = read_trips(csv, tz="America/New_York")
    >>> trips.loc[0, "member_type"], float(trips.loc[0, "duration_s"])
    ('casual', 300.0)
    """
    frames = list(iter_trips(path, fmt, tz=tz, network=network, chunksize=chunksize))
    if not frames:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=TRIP_COLUMNS)
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)

Short answers to a task, each a runnable example on synthetic data (they are executed by the test suite). They use the data-lake modules, which are experimental. For a first walk through the whole chain, see the tutorial.

I want to... Recipe know whether a collection is complete enough to use Check the quality of a collection turn a month of minute snapshots into 15-minute, hourly and daily tables Aggregate a month of snapshots hand a closed period to someone who must be able to trust it, for instance on Zenodo Freeze a version for Zenodo read the trip files an operator publishes Read published trips

docs.title: Aggregate a month of snapshots
docs.text:
Minute snapshots are too many to plot or join: give me one row per station and quarter of an hour. aggregate_levels returns 15-minute, hourly and daily tables whose columns mean the same thing every time, and checks that each one holds exactly the input rows.

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from gbfs_toolkit.aggregate import aggregate_levels, check_conservation
from gbfs_toolkit.store import write_lake

# A "month" of 20 stations, here 3 days at a poll a minute (86 400 rows) to keep the example quick.
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
t = pd.date_range("2026-03-27", periods=3 * 1440, freq="min", tz="UTC")   # across Paris's clock change
n = 20
rows = pd.DataFrame({
    "system_id": "demo",
    "station_id": np.repeat([f"s{i:02d}" for i in range(n)], len(t)),
    "observed_at_utc": np.tile(t, n),
    "num_bikes_available": rng.integers(0, 20, len(t) * n),
    "num_docks_available": rng.integers(0, 20, len(t) * n),
})
lake = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "lake"
write_lake(rows, lake)

# 1. From the lake folder itself: DuckDB if installed, otherwise window by window in pandas.
#    The result is the same either way. Local columns follow the clock change.
levels = aggregate_levels(lake, time_col="observed_at_utc", tz="Europe/Paris")
print({name: len(table) for name, table in levels.items()})
print(levels["1h"].loc[levels["1h"]["station_id"] == "s00",
                       ["bucket_start_utc", "bucket_start_local", "utc_offset_min", "n_obs"]].iloc[[0, -1]])

# 2. The property that makes the three tables one dataset.
check_conservation(levels["15m"], lake)
assert {int(table["n_obs"].sum()) for table in levels.values()} == {len(rows)}

# 3. Choose the engine when you must.
by_windows = aggregate_levels(lake, time_col="observed_at_utc", engine="pandas", chunk="12h")
assert int(by_windows["1d"]["n_obs"].sum()) == len(rows)

What the columns mean (definitions are fixed): n_obs all rows in the bucket, n_valid the rows with a bike count that are not flagged both_zero_suspect, then bikes_*, docks_*, pct_empty, pct_full, pct_renting over the valid rows, and movement_volume, an estimate of how many bikes moved that is not a trip count. See aggregate.

For a real month (a large system at a poll a minute is tens of millions of rows):

  • collect with fragments and compact each closed day (collect), or write a lake;
  • pass the folder (aggregate_levels("data/lake", time_col="observed_at_utc")), not a frame read from it;
  • on a small machine, GBFS_TOOLKIT_DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT=4GB (and GBFS_TOOLKIT_DUCKDB_THREADS) cap DuckDB, which spills to a temporary folder it removes afterwards;
  • aggregate_availability(lake, "15min", ...) gives a single level.

docs.title: Check the quality of a collection
docs.text:
Which days can I trust, which not, and why? assess answers per system and UTC day with one of four statuses (ok, partial, outage_collector, outage_operator) and an incident registry. It reads a lake, a folder of day files or a frame, and a folder is read in place, so a month of Paris is no harder than a day.

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from gbfs_toolkit.quality import STATUSES, assess, write_incidents
from gbfs_toolkit.store import write_lake

# A collection of two systems over three days. Everything stops for 5 hours on the 2nd (the
# collector was down); "lakeside" also loses its feed on the 3rd (the operator).
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
frames = []
for system in ("riverside", "lakeside"):
    t = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=3 * 1440, freq="min", tz="UTC")
    t = t[(t < "2026-03-02T02:00Z") | (t >= "2026-03-02T07:00Z")]
    if system == "lakeside":
        t = t[t < "2026-03-03T00:00Z"]
    frames.append(pd.DataFrame({
        "system_id": system, "station_id": "s1", "observed_at_utc": t,
        "num_bikes_available": rng.integers(0, 12, len(t)),
        "num_docks_available": rng.integers(0, 12, len(t)),
    }))
lake = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "lake"
write_lake(pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True), lake)

# 1. Assess the folder itself (nothing is loaded whole). Leave today out in real use: pass
#    end="<yesterday>", since a day still being collected is "partial".
report = assess(lake, time_col="observed_at_utc", end="2026-03-03")
print(report.coverage[["date_utc", "system_id", "completeness_pct", "status"]].to_string(index=False))

# 2. What happened? The gap and the silent feed were found and given stable identifiers.
print(report.incidents[["incident_id", "cause", "scope"]].to_string(index=False))
print(report.summary()["days_by_status"])

# 3. A gate for a script: the days you accept, and the days you must look at.
bad = report.coverage[report.coverage["status"] != "ok"]
print(f"{len(bad)} system-day(s) to look at")
assert set(report.coverage["status"]) <= set(STATUSES)

# 4. Keep the registry next to the data; add what only you know (a migration, a known fault).
write_incidents(report.incidents, lake.parent / "incidents.json")

Reading the statuses: ok is at least 95 % of the expected polls (ok_threshold_pct); outage_collector is a day that overlaps a stretch in which no system was polled (the collection's fault, not the operators'); outage_operator is a day with nothing from this system while others were collected; partial is anything else, with no explanation. The expected number of polls is one a minute (poll_resolution="15min" for 96 a day, or expected_polls=).

From a shell: gbfs quality data/lake --end 2026-03-31 --strict exits 1 if any system-day is not ok (command line). The same works on a collection folder (data/collected).

The three row-level indicators (add_quality_indicators) flag values that are ambiguous at the source (both_zero_suspect, a field an operator never publishes, a poll in which everything reads zero). They flag and never remove: what to do with a flagged row is your analysis's decision. They return a row per input row, so they take a frame: read the part you need with read_lake.

See also quality for every definition.

docs.title: Freeze a version for Zenodo
docs.text:
I have a closed period of a lake and I want a folder someone else can check. freeze_release cuts the data at the period, adds the daily coverage and incidents, a Frictionless datapackage.json, a Croissant file, a README and a SHA256SUMS. It uploads nothing and has no default licence: the licence is yours to choose, and the data are probably not only yours (a feed has its own terms).

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from gbfs_toolkit.release import freeze_release, verify_release
from gbfs_toolkit.repro import fingerprint
from gbfs_toolkit.store import write_lake

# A lake with two days of one system (synthetic).
t = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=2 * 1440, freq="min", tz="UTC")
snapshots = pd.DataFrame({"system_id": "alpha", "station_id": "s1", "observed_at_utc": t,
                          "num_bikes_available": 3, "num_docks_available": 5})
work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
write_lake(snapshots, work / "lake")

# 1. Freeze the closed period (the end must be in the past). State the licences you know.
info = freeze_release(
    work / "lake", work / "release", name="alpha-2026-03",
    start="2026-03-01", end="2026-03-02", license="CC-BY-4.0",
    title="Alpha bike share, station status, March 2026",
    producers=[{"system_id": "alpha", "producer": "City of Alpha", "license": "Open licence 2.0"}],
)
print(info["rows"], info["systems"], info["files"])
print(sorted(p.name for p in (work / "release").iterdir()))

# 2. Verify it as the person who downloads it would: every file against SHA256SUMS ...
print(verify_release(work / "release")["ok"])
# ... and the content (rows and fingerprint) against the manifest, which also catches a file that
# was re-encoded and re-checksummed.
print(verify_release(work / "release", deep=True)["ok"])

# 3. The fingerprint depends on the content, not on file layout or row order.
print(fingerprint(work / "release" / "data" / "station_status"))

Then, outside the library:

  1. read the generated README.md (it says what is and is not in the folder, and that there is no licence if you gave none);
  2. deposit the folder on Zenodo (or any repository) yourself;
  3. add the DOI Zenodo gives to your CITATION.cff, and keep the release's name and version in the paper's data statement.

From a shell: gbfs release data/lake releases/alpha-2026-03 --name alpha-2026-03 --start 2026-03-01 --end 2026-03-31 --license CC-BY-4.0 and gbfs verify releases/alpha-2026-03 --deep. A release is written once: the folder must not exist or must be empty. See release and repro.

docs.title: Read published trips
docs.text:
An operator publishes a trip file; I want one table, with times I can trust and no personal data. read_trips reads Lyft/Motivate files (Citi Bike, Divvy, Bluebikes...), Urban Sharing, Bicycle Transit Systems and the Vélomagg file of Montpellier into the same columns (TRIP_COLUMNS), and TripFormat describes any other. Nothing is guessed: a format is added when its columns have been checked on a real file.

import io

import pandas as pd

from gbfs_toolkit.trips import TRIP_COLUMNS, TripFormat, read_trips

# 1. A file that publishes local times without a zone: tz= is required (there is no default),
#    and the hours a clock change makes odd are flagged, not fixed silently.
current = (
    "ride_id,rideable_type,started_at,ended_at,start_station_id,end_station_id,member_casual\n"
    "r1,electric_bike,2024-03-10 01:50:00,2024-03-10 03:10:00,S1,S2,member\n"
    "r2,classic_bike,2024-11-03 01:30:00,2024-11-03 01:45:00,S2,,casual\n"
)
trips = read_trips(io.BytesIO(current.encode()), tz="America/New_York", network="demo")
print(trips[["ride_id", "started_at", "duration_s", "member_type", "started_at_tz_flag"]])

# 2. The Vélomagg file (Montpellier, open data): the station number is split from the name, text
#    that was encoded twice is repaired, the account column is never read, and the operator's own
#    staff flag is carried as a nullable boolean. (Two invented rows in the published shape.)
velomagg = (
    "Departure,Return,Bike,Departure station,Return station,Covered distance (m),Duration (sec.),"
    "Manager,new_account\n"
    "2025-06-01 08:00:00,2025-06-01 08:12:00,230,001 Place Exemple,002 CafÃ© de la Gare,2909,700,False,900001\n"
    "2025-06-01 09:00:00,2025-06-01 09:05:00,619,002 CafÃ© de la Gare,001 Place Exemple,800,290,True,900002\n"
)
rides = read_trips(io.BytesIO(velomagg.encode("utf-8")), tz="Europe/Paris", network="velomagg")
print(rides[["start_station_id", "end_station_name", "distance_m", "is_operator_staff"]])
assert list(rides.columns) == TRIP_COLUMNS and "900001" not in rides.astype(str).to_csv()

# 3. Another format: describe its columns once.
mine = TripFormat("mycity", {"ride_id": ["id"], "started_at": ["debut"], "ended_at": ["fin"]},
                  times_have_offset=True)
raw = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1], "debut": ["2025-01-01T10:00:00+01:00"], "fin": ["2025-01-01T10:05:00+01:00"]})
print(read_trips(io.BytesIO(raw.to_csv(index=False).encode()), mine)[["started_at", "duration_s"]])

Things to know:

  • Time zones. Times come out tz-aware UTC. started_at_tz_flag and ended_at_tz_flag say nonexistent (the skipped hour in spring) or ambiguous (the repeated hour in autumn).
  • No personal data. Birth year, gender, bike number and account number are dropped, and the schema has no user identifier. The Vélomagg account column cannot be kept. Times and stations combined can still identify someone: check the publisher's terms before releasing anything built from a trip file.
  • is_operator_staff is the publisher's flag for trips made by its own staff, carried as published; the other formats leave it empty. This module does nothing else with it.
  • Big files. iter_trips(path, tz=...) yields normalised chunks; a .zip (nested zips included) is read member by member.

See trips.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Every public object, generated from gbfs_toolkit.__all__ (so this catalogue is always complete). Use the search bar to jump straight to a function, or browse by theme below.

Start with the data model

Every function in this library consumes or returns the canonical, tz-aware UTC pandas frames described in Data model & schemas. Read it first: the column names and dtypes are the contract these functions rely on.

docs.title: Audit (A1–A7)
docs.text: Function Summary audit_catalogue Fetch and audit many systems with one call. audit_dynamic Logic checks on a live availability frame. audit_frames Unified semantic audit on canonical frames: static (A1–A7) and, if given, dynamic (D1–D3). audit_sensitivity One-at-a-time threshold sensitivity of the A1–A7 audit. audit_static Run the A1–A7 semantic audit on a canonical station-information frame. AuditReport The verdict of audit_static: a DataFrame with declared columns and a few readers. capacity_convention Label each system's capacity-field publication convention. classify_from_vehicle_types Feed-intrinsic car-sharing classification from GBFS v3 vehicle_types. classify_from_virtual_station Feed-intrinsic free-floating tagging from GBFS v3 is_virtual_station. drop_flagged The analysis-ready subset: stations that pass the static A1–A7 audit, in one call. flag_rate_ci System-level flag rate per class with a cluster-bootstrap confidence interval. flag_sentinel_coordinates Boolean mask of stations sitting on the (0, 0) null-island sentinel. overcapacity_ratio Per-system A3 over-capacity ratio from declared station capacity. reclassify_overcapacity Relabel over-capacity systems as free_floating (the audit protocol's S3 step). vehicle_id_persistence Characterise whether a feed rotates or persists its vehicle_id values.

docs.title: Analytics
docs.text: Function Summary aliasing_vulnerability Per-station risk that the polling cadence misses short-timescale dynamics. availability_stats Per-station longitudinal statistics from an availability panel. availability_synchrony Pairwise correlation of station availability series: a functional synchrony network. block_bootstrap_ci Moving-block bootstrap confidence interval for a statistic of a dependent series. boundary_stress Per-station share of time near empty or near full, not just at the boundary. capacity_utilization Add utilization_rate = available bikes / station capacity. censored_time_ratio Fraction of station-time at a saturation boundary, where demand is unobservable. cluster_diurnal_profiles Cluster stations by their daily rhythm (the crown jewel of the longitudinal layer). cluster_spatial Group stations into spatial zones by physical proximity. cluster_spectral Topological clustering: geographic kNN affinity → Laplacian spectrum → k-means. cohen_kappa Cohen's kappa between two raters over paired nominal labels. compare_systems Stack system_profile across many systems into a comparison table. concentration_metrics How concentrated is capacity across stations? An equity / coverage lens. cumulative_imbalance Per-station cumulative net flow (drift) since each period's start. cyclical_time_features Encode calendar fields as (sin, cos) pairs: the one everyone re-implements. detect_ghost_vehicles Flag immobile ("ghost") vehicles from a longitudinal vehicle panel. diurnal_bimodality Sarle's bimodality coefficient of each station's diurnal profile. diurnal_profiles Build each station's mean occupancy profile by hour of day. diurnal_summary_stats Hour-of-day summary of a quantity: mean, median and robust P5/P95 bands. docking_pressure Per-observation docking saturation tension: typical inflow over free docks. dynamic_gini_index Gini coefficient of available bikes across stations, as a time series. ebikes Electric vehicles only (any
